## P3 - `Remove File` before the follow test fails on a clean runner in [`tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/d5b3e9a76678dca8b93b81a533d3ad32a5b28183/tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot#L1-L1)

**Location:** [tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot:46-47](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/d5b3e9a76678dca8b93b81a533d3ad32a5b28183/tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot#L46-L47)

**Problem:** The new &#39;Logs follow streams new lines&#39; test starts with an unguarded `Remove File ${follow-log}` where `${follow-log}` is `/tmp/clab-logs-follow.log`. Robot Framework&#39;s built-in `Remove File` fails when the file does not exist, and nothing in the suite creates the file before this point. The same PR guards identical pre-clean steps elsewhere&#58; [`tests/14-clabernetes/01-linux-lifecycle.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/d5b3e9a76678dca8b93b81a533d3ad32a5b28183/tests/14-clabernetes/01-linux-lifecycle.robot#L1-L1) defines `Remove File If Exists`, and this suite&#39;s `Cleanup` keyword wraps `Remove File` in `Run Keyword And Ignore Error`.

**Trigger:** Any first run of the `32*.robot` suite on a clean GitHub Actions runner, where `/tmp` is empty and the follow log does not yet exist.

**Impact:** The follow test case fails on every clean execution, so the smoke job this PR wires into [`smoke-tests.yml`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/d5b3e9a76678dca8b93b81a533d3ad32a5b28183/.github/workflows/smoke-tests.yml#L1-L1) fails until a stale log from a prior run masks the issue.

**Suggested correction:** Guard the pre-clean the same way the rest of the suite does&#58; `Run Keyword And Ignore Error    Remove File    ${follow-log}` or reuse a `Remove File If Exists` user keyword at line 47.


## P4 - `clientLoader.byIdentity` caches one Kubernetes client set per identity with no eviction

**Location:** [labruntime/clabernetes/clabernetes.go:137-181](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/d5b3e9a76678dca8b93b81a533d3ad32a5b28183/labruntime/clabernetes/clabernetes.go#L137-L181)

**Problem:** `load` stores a `kubeClients` entry &#40;dynamic client, typed clientset, copied `rest.Config`&#41; per `identityKey` in `byIdentity` with no size bound or eviction.

**Trigger:** A long-lived `Runtime` acting as many distinct identities. The docs name multi-user servers as the consumer of `WithLabRuntimeIdentity`; if such a server reuses one `CLab` across calls instead of constructing one per request, the map grows for the process lifetime. CLI usage and per-`CLab` construction keep it small.

**Impact:** Unbounded memory growth and idle connections only in the long-lived, many-identities deployment shape; not a CLI defect.

**Suggested correction:** Cap the cache &#40;small LRU keyed by `identityKey`&#41;, evict stale entries, or document in the `clientLoader` comment that the cache assumes a bounded identity set per runtime lifetime.


## P4 - `SampleStats` lists `PodMetrics` for the whole namespace instead of per pod

**Location:** [labruntime/clabernetes/access.go:452-466](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/d5b3e9a76678dca8b93b81a533d3ad32a5b28183/labruntime/clabernetes/access.go#L452-L466)

**Problem:** The metrics list uses `metav1.ListOptions{}` with no narrowing; every pod in the namespace is fetched and only the lab&#39;s pods are consumed. `PodMetrics` objects carry no user labels, so a label selector cannot filter by the lab.

**Trigger:** Stats sampling in a namespace shared by many labs or other workloads. With the default dedicated-namespace-per-lab setup the list is bounded by the lab&#39;s own pods.

**Impact:** Extra transfer and per-call work proportional to all pods in a shared namespace, repeated on each stats sample; minor today, larger only for shared-namespace deployments.

**Suggested correction:** Fetch metrics per pod with `Resource(podMetricsGVR).Namespace(ns).Get(ctx, podName, ...)` for the lab&#39;s known pods, or keep the list and note the shared-namespace tradeoff in the method comment.


## Coverage

- Source-only review&#58; no tests, builds, or linters were executed; all findings are from code and test-file inspection.
- All 38 changed paths in the diff were read; head files for the CLI, core access layer, c9s runtime, docker, and podman were inspected directly.
- Podman `WriteContainerLogs` was verified correct&#58; all channel sends happen before `done` is sent, and `drain()` only runs on the write-error path.
- Identity flow verified end-to-end&#58; every new access operation connects with `req.Identity`, internal `Inspect` calls resolve a zero identity to the connected view&#39;s identity, and websocket/SPDY transports are built from the impersonated rest config.
- The Robot Framework fail-on-missing-file behavior of `Remove File` is external knowledge; the P3 finding is calibrated to that confidence and corroborated by the suite&#39;s own `Remove File If Exists` pattern.
- The metrics-server v0.9.0 `components.yaml` URL and its kind compatibility could not be verified from the repository.
- The `clientLoader` growth assessment assumes per-CLab construction for multi-user servers; the out-of-repo clab-api-server usage pattern could not be inspected here.
- Dropped candidates&#58; `identityKey` NUL collision is practically unreachable because HTTP header impersonation cannot carry NUL; `newExecutor` building both transports mirrors kubectl&#39;s fallback pattern; podman drain concern was resolved as correct.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

162: +		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
163: +			return logsFn(cmd, o)
164: +		},
165: +	}
166: +
167: +	c.Flags().StringVarP(
168: +		&o.Logs.Node,
169: +		"node",
170: +		"n",
171: +		o.Logs.Node,
172: +		"node to show the logs of",
173: +	)
174: +	c.Flags().Int64Var(
175: +		&o.Logs.Tail,
176: +		"tail",
177: +		o.Logs.Tail,
178: +		"number of lines to show from the end of the log; -1 shows the whole log",
179: +	)
180: +	c.Flags().BoolVarP(
181: +		&o.Logs.Follow,
182: +		"follow",
183: +		"f",
184: +		o.Logs.Follow,
185: +		"keep streaming new log lines",
186: +	)
187: +	c.Flags().BoolVar(
188: +		&o.Logs.Timestamps,
189: +		"timestamps",
190: +		o.Logs.Timestamps,
191: +		"prefix every line with its timestamp",
192: +	)
193: +
194: +	c.Example = `# Show the whole log of node srl1
195: +containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1
196: +
197: +# Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps
198: +containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps`
199: +
200: +	return c, nil
201: +}
202: +
203: +func logsFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
204: +	if o.Global.TopologyName == "" && o.Global.TopologyFile == "" {
205: +		return fmt.Errorf("provide either a lab name (--name) or a topology file path (--topo)")
206: +	}
207: +	if o.Logs.Node == "" {
208: +		return fmt.Errorf("provide the node to show the logs of (--node)")
209: +	}
210: +
211: +	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
212: +	if err != nil {
213: +		return err
214: +	}
215: +
216: +	opts := clabcore.NodeLogOptions{
217: +		NodeName:   o.Logs.Node,
218: +		Follow:     o.Logs.Follow,
219: +		Timestamps: o.Logs.Timestamps,
220: +	}
221: +	if o.Logs.Tail >= 0 {
222: +		tail := o.Logs.Tail
223: +		opts.Tail = &tail
224: +	}
225: +
226: +	return c.NodeLogs(cmd.Context(), opts, cmd.OutOrStdout(), cmd.ErrOrStderr())
227: +}

572: new file mode 100644
573: index 0000000..e69b042
574: --- /dev/null
575: +++ b/core/labruntime_access.go
576: @@ -0,0 +1,246 @@
577: +package core
578: +
579: +import (
580: +	"context"
581: +	"fmt"
582: +	"io"
583: +	"net"
584: +	"sort"
585: +
586: +	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
587: +	clablabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime"
588: +	clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"
589: +	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
590: +)
591: +
592: +// The helpers in this file give library users per-node access to the lab selected by the CLab
593: +// (its topology file or WithTopologyName). Node names are accepted as the topology file spells
594: +// them or as a lab runtime sanitized them. Lab runtime calls act as the identity set with
595: +// WithLabRuntimeIdentity.
596: +
597: +// LocateLabRuntimeNodes reports the workload (namespace, pod, primary device container, Node
598: +// UID, exposed ports) of the given nodes, or of every node of the lab when none are given.
599: +func (c *CLab) LocateLabRuntimeNodes(
600: +	ctx context.Context,
601: +	nodeNames ...string,
602: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
603: +	locator, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLocator](c, "locating nodes")
604: +	if err != nil {
605: +		return nil, err
606: +	}
607: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
608: +		return nil, err
609: +	}
610: +
611: +	return locator.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
612: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
613: +		Nodes:    nodeNames,
614: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
615: +	})
616: +}
617: +
618: +// AttachLabRuntimeNode runs an interactive command in a node's device container (or in
619: +// req.Container) with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing. The lab name and identity
620: +// default to the CLab's. A command exiting nonzero returns a *labruntime.CommandExitError.
621: +func (c *CLab) AttachLabRuntimeNode(
622: +	ctx context.Context,
623: +	req clablabruntime.AttachRequest,
624: +	streams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,
625: +) error {
626: +	attacher, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeAttacher](c, "attaching to nodes")
627: +	if err != nil {
628: +		return err
629: +	}
630: +
631: +	if req.Name == "" {
632: +		if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
633: +			return err
634: +		}
635: +		req.Name = c.Config.Name
636: +	}
637: +	if req.Identity.IsZero() {
638: +		req.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity
639: +	}
640: +
641: +	return attacher.Attach(ctx, req, streams)
642: +}
643: +
644: +// DialLabRuntimeNodePort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node (SSH, web UIs) through the
645: +// lab runtime, such as a Kubernetes port-forward.
646: +func (c *CLab) DialLabRuntimeNodePort(
647: +	ctx context.Context,
648: +	nodeName string,
649: +	port int,
650: +) (net.Conn, error) {
651: +	forwarder, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodePortForwarder](
652: +		c, "port-forwarding to nodes")
653: +	if err != nil {
654: +		return nil, err
655: +	}
656: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
657: +		return nil, err
658: +	}
659: +
660: +	return forwarder.DialPort(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
661: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
662: +		Nodes:    []string{nodeName},
663: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
664: +	}, port)
665: +}
666: +
667: +// SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats reports the CPU and memory usage of the lab's running nodes. It
668: +// returns an error wrapping labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable when the cluster serves no resource
669: +// metrics.
670: +func (c *CLab) SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats(ctx context.Context) ([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, error) {
671: +	sampler, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeStatsSampler](
672: +		c, "sampling node stats")
673: +	if err != nil {
674: +		return nil, err
675: +	}
676: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
677: +		return nil, err
678: +	}
679: +
680: +	return sampler.SampleStats(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
681: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
682: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
683: +	})
684: +}
685: +
686: +// NodeLogOptions selects the node log NodeLogs writes.
687: +type NodeLogOptions struct {
688: +	// NodeName is the node whose log is written.
689: +	NodeName string
690: +	// Container overrides a lab runtime node's primary device container. Local runtimes do
691: +	// not support it.
692: +	Container string
693: +	// Tail limits the output to the last lines of the log; nil writes the whole log.
694: +	Tail *int64
695: +	// Follow keeps writing new log lines until the context ends.
696: +	Follow bool
697: +	// Timestamps prefixes every line with its timestamp.
698: +	Timestamps bool
699: +}
700: +
701: +// NodeLogs writes the log of a lab node with every runtime: the container log with Docker and
702: +// Podman, the device container log with a lab runtime. Lab runtimes write one combined stream to
703: +// stdout.
704: +func (c *CLab) NodeLogs(
705: +	ctx context.Context,
706: +	opts NodeLogOptions,
707: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
708: +) error {
709: +	if opts.NodeName == "" {
710: +		return fmt.Errorf("node name is required")
711: +	}
712: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
713: +		return err
714: +	}
715: +
716: +	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
717: +		streamer, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLogStreamer](
718: +			c, "streaming node logs")
719: +		if err != nil {
720: +			return err
721: +		}
722: +
723: +		return streamer.StreamLogs(ctx, clablabruntime.LogRequest{
724: +			Name:       c.Config.Name,
725: +			NodeName:   opts.NodeName,
726: +			Container:  opts.Container,
727: +			Tail:       opts.Tail,
728: +			Follow:     opts.Follow,
729: +			Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
730: +			Identity:   c.labRuntimeIdentity,
731: +		}, stdout)
732: +	}
733: +
734: +	if opts.Container != "" {
735: +		return fmt.Errorf("selecting a container is only supported with lab runtimes")
736: +	}
737: +
738: +	runtime, containerName, err := c.nodeContainer(ctx, opts.NodeName)
739: +	if err != nil {
740: +		return err
741: +	}
742: +
743: +	writer, ok := runtime.(clabruntime.ContainerLogWriter)
744: +	if !ok {
745: +		return fmt.Errorf("container runtime %q does not support node logs", runtime.GetName())
746: +	}
747: +
748: +	return writer.WriteContainerLogs(ctx, containerName, clabruntime.ContainerLogOptions{
749: +		Tail:       opts.Tail,
750: +		Follow:     opts.Follow,
751: +		Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
752: +	}, stdout, stderr)
753: +}
754: +
755: +// nodeContainer finds the container of a lab node in the local container runtimes by the lab
756: +// and node name labels.
757: +func (c *CLab) nodeContainer(
758: +	ctx context.Context,
759: +	nodeName string,
760: +) (clabruntime.ContainerRuntime, string, error) {
761: +	filters := []*clabtypes.GenericFilter{
762: +		{
763: +			FilterType: "label",
764: +			Field:      clabconstants.Containerlab,
765: +			Operator:   "=",
766: +			Match:      c.Config.Name,
767: +		},
768: +		{
769: +			FilterType: "label",
770: +			Field:      clabconstants.NodeName,
771: +			Operator:   "=",
772: +			Match:      nodeName,
773: +		},
774: +	}
775: +
776: +	runtimeNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Runtimes))
777: +	for name := range c.Runtimes {
778: +		runtimeNames = append(runtimeNames, name)
779: +	}
780: +	sort.Strings(runtimeNames)
781: +
782: +	for _, name := range runtimeNames {
783: +		runtime := c.Runtimes[name]
784: +
785: +		containers, err := runtime.ListContainers(ctx, filters)
786: +		if err != nil {
787: +			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("could not list containers: %w", err)
788: +		}
789: +		if len(containers) != 0 && len(containers[0].Names) != 0 {
790: +			return runtime, containers[0].Names[0], nil
791: +		}
792: +	}
793: +
794: +	return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: node %q of lab %q has no container",
795: +		ErrNodeNotFound, nodeName, c.Config.Name)
796: +}
797: +
798: +func (c *CLab) requireLabName() error {
799: +	if c.Config == nil || c.Config.Name == "" {
800: +		return fmt.Errorf("provide a lab name (--name) or a topology file (--topo)")
801: +	}
802: +
803: +	return nil
804: +}
805: +
806: +// labRuntimeCapability returns the CLab's lab runtime as an optional lab runtime interface.
807: +func labRuntimeCapability[T any](c *CLab, operation string) (T, error) {
808: +	var zero T
809: +
810: +	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
811: +		return zero, fmt.Errorf("%s needs a lab runtime such as %q",
812: +			operation, clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName)
813: +	}
814: +
815: +	capability, ok := c.LabRuntime.(T)
816: +	if !ok {
817: +		return zero, fmt.Errorf("lab runtime %q does not support %s",
818: +			c.globalRuntimeName, operation)
819: +	}
820: +
821: +	return capability, nil
822: +}

1042: +func TestNodeLogsWithALocalRuntime(t *testing.T) {
1043: +	t.Parallel()
1044: +
1045: +	ctrl := gomock.NewController(t)
1046: +	mock := clabmocksmockruntime.NewMockContainerRuntime(ctrl)
1047: +	mock.EXPECT().ListContainers(gomock.Any(), gomock.Any()).DoAndReturn(
1048: +		func(_ context.Context, filters []*clabtypes.GenericFilter) (
1049: +			[]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error,
1050: +		) {
1051: +			labels := map[string]string{}
1052: +			for _, filter := range filters {
1053: +				labels[filter.Field] = filter.Match
1054: +			}
1055: +			if labels[clabconstants.Containerlab] != "lab1" {
1056: +				return nil, nil
1057: +			}
1058: +			if labels[clabconstants.NodeName] != "r1" {
1059: +				return nil, nil
1060: +			}
1061: +
1062: +			return []clabruntime.GenericContainer{{Names: []string{"clab-lab1-r1"}}}, nil
1063: +		}).
1064: +		AnyTimes()
1065: +
1066: +	runtime := &logWritingRuntime{MockContainerRuntime: mock}
1067: +	c := &CLab{
1068: +		Config:   &Config{Name: "lab1"},
1069: +		Runtimes: map[string]clabruntime.ContainerRuntime{"docker": runtime},
1070: +	}
1071: +
1072: +	var stdout, stderr strings.Builder
1073: +	if err := c.NodeLogs(context.Background(), NodeLogOptions{NodeName: "r1", Follow: true},
1074: +		&stdout, &stderr); err != nil {
1075: +		t.Fatal(err)
1076: +	}
1077: +	if runtime.containerName != "clab-lab1-r1" || !runtime.opts.Follow ||
1078: +		runtime.opts.Tail != nil ||
1079: +		stdout.String() != "out\n" ||
1080: +		stderr.String() != "err\n" {
1081: +		t.Fatalf("container %q opts %+v stdout %q stderr %q",
1082: +			runtime.containerName, runtime.opts, stdout.String(), stderr.String())
1083: +	}
1084: +
1085: +	err := c.NodeLogs(context.Background(), NodeLogOptions{NodeName: "missing"},
1086: +		io.Discard, io.Discard)
1087: +	if !errors.Is(err, ErrNodeNotFound) {
1088: +		t.Fatalf("missing node error = %v", err)
1089: +	}
1090: +
1091: +	if err := c.NodeLogs(context.Background(), NodeLogOptions{NodeName: "r1", Container: "x"},
1092: +		io.Discard, io.Discard); err == nil {
1093: +		t.Fatal("a container override was accepted for a local runtime")
1094: +	}
1095: +}

1136: +// (ghcr.io/srl-labs/network-multitool). With CLAB_C9S_TEST_USER set, every call impersonates
1137: +// that user, who must be allowed to read the lab and use pods/exec, pods/portforward and
1138: +// pods/log in its namespace; CLAB_C9S_TEST_FORBIDDEN_USER names a user without these rights.

1153: +	}

1157: +

1160: +		if err != nil {

1162: +		}
1163: +		if len(locations) != 1 || locations[0].Pod == "" || locations[0].Container == "" ||
1164: +			locations[0].NodeUID == "" {

1166: +		}
1167: +	})
1168: +
1169: +	t.Run("attach with a terminal", func(t *testing.T) {
1170: +		resize := make(chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize, 1)
1171: +		resize <- clablabruntime.TerminalSize{Width: 101, Height: 33}
1172: +
1173: +		var out bytes.Buffer
1174: +		err := c.AttachLabRuntimeNode(ctx, clablabruntime.AttachRequest{
1175: +			NodeName: "client",
1176: +			Command:  []string{"sh", "-c", "sleep 1; stty size; echo attached-$((6*7))"},
1177: +			TTY:      true,
1178: +		}, clablabruntime.AttachStreams{Stdout: &out, Resize: resize})
1179: +		if err != nil {

1182: +		if !strings.Contains(out.String(), "33 101") ||

1185: +		}
1186: +	})
1187: +

1189: +		var out bytes.Buffer

1191: +			NodeName: "client",
1192: +			Command:  []string{"cat"},
1193: +		}, clablabruntime.AttachStreams{
1194: +			Stdin:  strings.NewReader("hello from stdin\n"),
1195: +			Stdout: &out,
1196: +			Stderr: io.Discard,
1197: +		})
1198: +		if err != nil {
1199: +			t.Fatal(err)
1200: +		}

1203: +		}
1204: +	})

1211: +
1212: +		var exitErr *clablabruntime.CommandExitError
1213: +		if !errors.As(err, &exitErr) || exitErr.Code != 3 {
1214: +			t.Fatalf("exit error = %v, want code 3", err)
1215: +		}
1216: +	})
1217: +

1347: new file mode 100644
1348: index 0000000..c7567dc
1349: --- /dev/null
1350: +++ b/docs/cmd/logs.md
1351: @@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
1352: +# logs command
1353: +
1354: +### Description
1355: +
1356: +The `logs` command shows the log of a lab node. With Docker and Podman it is the node container's log, with the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#logs) the log of the node's primary device container in its pod.
1357: +
1358: +--8<-- "docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags"
1359: +
1360: +### Usage
1361: +
1362: +`containerlab [global-flags] logs [local-flags]`
1363: +
1364: +### Flags
1365: +
1366: +#### topology | name
1367: +
1368: +Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.
1369: +
1370: +#### node
1371: +
1372: +Use the local `--node | -n` flag to select the node. The flag is required. With the c9s runtime the node name is accepted as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`).
1373: +
1374: +#### tail
1375: +
1376: +The local `--tail` flag limits the output to the last N lines of the log. The default `-1` shows the whole log; `--tail 0` shows no previous lines, which is useful with `--follow`.
1377: +
1378: +#### follow
1379: +
1380: +The local `--follow | -f` flag keeps streaming new log lines until the command is interrupted.
1381: +
1382: +#### timestamps
1383: +
1384: +The local `--timestamps` flag prefixes every line with its timestamp in RFC 3339 format.
1385: +
1386: +### Output
1387: +
1388: +The log goes to stdout. With Docker and Podman, the container's stderr goes to stderr, unless the container has a TTY; Kubernetes returns one combined stream, written to stdout.
1389: +
1390: +### Examples
1391: +
1392: +#### Show the whole log of a node
1393: +
1394: +```bash
1395: +containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1
1396: +```
1397: +
1398: +#### Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps
1399: +
1400: +```bash
1401: +containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps
1402: +```
1403: +
1404: +#### Show the device log of a node in a c9s lab
1405: +
1406: +```bash
1407: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 50
1408: +```

1410: index 88e63a4..18dc015 100644
1411: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
1412: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
1413: @@ -528,10 +528,24 @@ needs to reach the cluster.
1414:  If any selected command returns nonzero, or pod exec itself fails, the outer
1415:  `containerlab exec` also returns nonzero. Successful and failed results that
1416:  were received are still printed, so automation can use both the output and the
1417:  process exit status.
1418:  
1419: +## Logs
1420: +
1421: +`logs` shows the log of a node's primary device container, the same container
1422: +`exec` uses:
1423: +
1424: +```bash
1425: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs -t topo.clab.yml -n srl1
1426: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps
1427: +```
1428: +
1429: +It reads the `pods/log` subresource of the node's pod, so RBAC must allow
1430: +`get` on `pods/log`. Kubernetes returns stdout and stderr as one stream. See
1431: +the [`logs` command](../../cmd/logs.md) for the flags.
1432: +
1433:  ## Start, stop, and restart
1434:  
1435:  Node lifecycle commands operate on the kubernetes Deployments created by
1436:  Clabernetes.
1437:  
1438: @@ -782,10 +796,66 @@ token:
1439:  ```bash
1440:  kubectl -n <namespace> annotate node.c9s.run <node> \
1441:    c9s.run/device-state-reset=$(date +%s) --overwrite
1442:  ```
1443:  
1444: +## Node access from Go
1445: +
1446: +Programs that use containerlab as a Go library, such as clab-api-server, open
1447: +terminals, follow logs, reach node ports and read resource usage through
1448: +optional lab runtime interfaces in `github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime`,
1449: +implemented by the c9s runtime:
1450: +
1451: +| Interface | Method | What it does |
1452: +|---|---|---|
1453: +| `NodeLocator` | `LocateNode(ctx, NodeRequest) ([]NodeLocation, error)` | the namespace, pod, primary device container, Node UID, exposed ports and LoadBalancer address of nodes |
1454: +| `NodeAttacher` | `Attach(ctx, AttachRequest, AttachStreams) error` | an interactive exec with stdin, an optional TTY and a resize channel, in the device container or a chosen container |
1455: +| `NodeLogStreamer` | `StreamLogs(ctx, LogRequest, io.Writer) error` | the device container log, with tail, follow and timestamps |
1456: +| `NodePortForwarder` | `DialPort(ctx, NodeRequest, port) (net.Conn, error)` | a connection to a TCP port of the node's pod through `pods/portforward` (SSH, web UIs) |
1457: +| `NodeStatsSampler` | `SampleStats(ctx, InspectRequest) ([]NodeStats, error)` | CPU and memory per node from `metrics.k8s.io` PodMetrics, summing the node's device containers; without the metrics API the error wraps `labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable` |
1458: +
1459: +The `core` package wraps them per lab and node name, accepting the node name
1460: +as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized:
1461: +`CLab.LocateLabRuntimeNodes`, `CLab.AttachLabRuntimeNode`,
1462: +`CLab.DialLabRuntimeNodePort`, `CLab.SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats` and
1463: +`CLab.NodeLogs`, which also serves Docker and Podman.
1464: +
1465: +```go
1466: +c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(
1467: +	clabcore.WithRuntime("c9s", nil),
1468: +	clabcore.WithTopologyName("clos"),
1469: +	clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity(clablabruntime.Identity{
1470: +		User:   "clab:alice",
1471: +		Groups: []string{"clab:users"},
1472: +	}),
1473: +)
1474: +if err != nil {
1475: +	return err
1476: +}
1477: +
1478: +conn, err := c.DialLabRuntimeNodePort(ctx, "srl1", 22)
1479: +```
1480: +
1481: +### Acting as a user
1482: +
1483: +A server that runs labs for many users acts as each user, so the cluster's RBAC
1484: +decides what a user may do and its audit log names the user:
1485: +
1486: +- `labruntime.Identity{User, Groups}` is Kubernetes user impersonation.
1487: +  `labruntime.Config.Identity` sets it for a runtime, every request type has an
1488: +  `Identity` field that overrides it per call, and
1489: +  `clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity` sets it for every call of a `CLab`.
1490: +- The c9s runtime builds one set of Kubernetes clients per identity from the
1491: +  kubeconfig and caches them. The impersonation applies to every transport:
1492: +  REST calls, watches, log streams, and the websocket and SPDY connections of
1493: +  exec, attach and port-forward.
1494: +- Without an identity, the kubeconfig is used as it is. The CLI has no
1495: +  impersonation flags: a CLI user acts with their own kubeconfig rights.
1496: +
1497: +The kubeconfig identity then needs the `impersonate` verb on the users and
1498: +groups it acts as.
1499: +
1500:  ## RBAC requirements
1501:  
1502:  The kube identity used by the outer containerlab process must be able to:
1503:  
1504:  - get, create, and delete namespaces when using automatic per-lab namespaces
1505: @@ -796,10 +866,13 @@ The kube identity used by the outer containerlab process must be able to:
1506:  - list and watch Pods
1507:  - list, get, and update Deployments
1508:  - create, get, list, update, and delete ConfigMaps used for local files
1509:  - exec into device Pods with `pods/exec`
1510:  - list and delete PersistentVolumeClaims for `destroy --cleanup`
1511: +- read container logs with `pods/log` for `logs`
1512: +- port-forward with `pods/portforward` for `NodePortForwarder`
1513: +- list `pods.metrics.k8s.io` for `NodeStatsSampler`
1514:  
1515:  Useful checks:
1516:  
1517:  ```bash
1518:  kubectl auth can-i get namespaces

With the c9s runtime the node name is accepted as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`).\n1373: +\n1374: +#### tail\n1375: +\n1376: +The local `--tail` flag limits the output to the last N lines of the log. The default `-1` shows the whole log; `--tail 0` shows no previous lines, which is useful with `--follow`.\n1377: +\n1378: +#### follow\n1379: +\n1380: +The local `--follow | -f` flag keeps streaming new log lines until the command is interrupted.\n1381: +\n1382: +#### timestamps\n1383: +\n1384: +The local `--timestamps` flag prefixes every line with its timestamp in RFC 3339 format.\n1385: +\n1386: +### Output\n1387: +\n1388: +The log goes to stdout. With Docker and Podman, the container's stderr goes to stderr, unless the container has a TTY; Kubernetes returns one combined stream, written to stdout.\n1389: +\n1390: +### Examples\n1391: +\n1392: +#### Show the whole log of a node\n1393: +\n1394: +```bash\n1395: +containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1\n1396: +```\n1397: +\n1398: +#### Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps\n1399: +\n1400: +```bash\n1401: +containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps\n1402: +```\n1403: +\n1404: +#### Show the device log of a node in a c9s lab\n1405: +\n1406: +```bash\n1407: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 50\n1408: +```\n1409: diff --git a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n1410: index 88e63a4..18dc015 100644\n1411: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n1412: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n1413: @@ -528,10 +528,24 @@ needs to reach the cluster.\n1414:  If any selected command returns nonzero, or pod exec itself fails, the outer\n1415:  `containerlab exec` also returns nonzero. See\n1431: +the [`logs` command](../../cmd/logs.md) for the flags.\n1432: +\n1433:  ## Start, stop, and restart\n1434:  \n1435:  Node lifecycle commands operate on the kubernetes Deployments created by\n1436:  Clabernetes.\n1437:  \n1438: @@ -782,10 +796,66 @@ token:\n1439:  ```bash\n1440:  kubectl -n <namespace> annotate node.c9s.run <node> \\\n1441:    c9s.run/device-state-reset=$(date +%s) --overwrite\n1442:  ```\n1443:  \n1444: +## Node access from Go\n1445: +\n1446: +Programs that use containerlab as a Go library, such as clab-api-server, open\n1447: +terminals, follow logs, reach node ports and read resource usage through\n1448: +optional lab runtime interfaces in `github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime`,\n1449: +implemented by the c9s runtime:\n1450: +\n1451: +| Interface | Method | What it does |\n1452: +|---|---|---|\n1453: +| `NodeLocator` | `LocateNode(ctx, NodeRequest) ([]NodeLocation, error)` | the namespace, pod, primary device container, Node UID, exposed ports and LoadBalancer address of nodes |\n1454: +| `NodeAttacher` | `Attach(ctx, AttachRequest, AttachStreams) error` | an interactive exec with stdin, an optional TTY and a resize channel, in the device container or a chosen container |\n1455: +| `NodeLogStreamer` | `StreamLogs(ctx, LogRequest, io.Writer) error` | the device container log, with tail, follow and timestamps |\n1456: +| `NodePortForwarder` | `DialPort(ctx, NodeRequest, port) (net.Conn, error)` | a connection to a TCP port of the node's pod through `pods/portforward` (SSH, web UIs) |\n1457: +| `NodeStatsSampler` | `SampleStats(ctx, InspectRequest) ([]NodeStats, error)` | CPU and memory per node from `metrics.k8s.io` PodMetrics, summing the node's device containers; without the metrics API the error wraps `labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable` |\n1458: +\n1459: +The `core` package wraps them per lab and node name, accepting the node name\n1460: +as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized:\n1461: +`CLab.LocateLabRuntimeNodes`, `CLab.AttachLabRuntimeNode`,\n1462: +`CLab.DialLabRuntimeNodePort`, `CLab.SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats` and\n1463: +`CLab.NodeLogs`, which also serves Docker and Podman.\n1464: +\n1465: +```go\n1466: +c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(\n1467: +\tclabcore.WithRuntime(\"c9s\", nil),\n1468: +\tclabcore.WithTopologyName(\"clos\"),\n1469: +\tclabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity(clablabruntime.Identity{\n1470: +\t\tUser:   \"clab:alice\",\n1471: +\t\tGroups: []string{\"clab:users\"},\n1472: +\t}),\n1473: +)\n1474: +if err != nil {\n1475: +\treturn err\n1476: +}\n1477: +\n1478: +conn, err := c.DialLabRuntimeNodePort(ctx, \"srl1\", 22)\n1479: +```\n1480: +\n1481: +### Acting as a user\n1482: +\n1483: +A server that runs labs for many users acts as each user, so the cluster's RBAC\n1484: +decides what a user may do and its audit log names the user:\n1485: +\n1486: +- `labruntime.Identity{User, Groups}` is Kubernetes user impersonation.\n1487: +  `labruntime.Config.Identity` sets it for a runtime, every request type has an\n1488: +  `Identity` field that overrides it per call, and\n1489: +  `clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity` sets it for every call of a `CLab`.\n1490: +- The c9s runtime builds one set of Kubernetes clients per identity from the\n1491: +  kubeconfig and caches them. The impersonation applies to every transport:\n1492: +  REST calls, watches, log streams, and the websocket and SPDY connections of\n1493: +  exec, attach and port-forward.\n1494: +- Without an identity, the kubeconfig is used as it is. 1598: +// LocateNode reports the pod, primary device container, Node UID and exposed ports of the
1599: +// requested nodes, or of every node of the lab when the request names none. Node names are
1600: +// accepted as the topology or as the cluster spells them.
1601: +func (r *Runtime) LocateNode(
1602: +	ctx context.Context,
1603: +	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
1604: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
1605: +	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
1606: +	if err != nil {
1607: +		return nil, err
1608: +	}
1609: +
1610: +	state, err := r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
1611: +		Name:      req.Name,
1612: +		Namespace: req.Namespace,
1613: +	})
1614: +	if err != nil {
1615: +		return nil, err
1616: +	}
1617: +
1618: +	nodes := make(map[string]clablabruntime.NodeState, len(state.Nodes))
1619: +	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
1620: +		nodes[node.Name] = node
1621: +	}
1622: +
1623: +	if len(req.Nodes) == 0 {
1624: +		locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(state.Nodes))
1625: +		for _, node := range state.Nodes {
1626: +			locations = append(locations, nodeLocation(state, node))
1627: +		}
1628: +
1629: +		return locations, nil
1630: +	}
1631: +
1632: +	locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(req.Nodes))
1633: +	for _, nodeName := range req.Nodes {
1634: +		resolved, ok := resolveKnownNodeName(nodes, nodeName)
1635: +		if !ok {
1636: +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("node %q was not found in c9s lab %s/%s",
1637: +				nodeName, state.Namespace, state.Name)
1638: +		}
1639: +		locations = append(locations, nodeLocation(state, nodes[resolved]))
1640: +	}
1641: +
1642: +	return locations, nil
1643: +}

1672: +	}

1735: +			Stderr:    stderr != nil,

1752: +	}

1759: +	}

1763: +	}

1766: +}

1768: +// newExecutor streams a pod exec over websockets, falling back to SPDY when the API server
1769: +// does not upgrade the websocket, like kubectl. The websocket executor reports upgrade
1770: +// failures with the k8s.io/streaming error types. Both transports are built from the runtime's
1771: +// rest config, so they carry its impersonation headers.
1772: +func (r *Runtime) newExecutor(execURL *url.URL) (remotecommand.Executor, error) {
1773: +	websocketExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewWebSocketExecutor(
1774: +		r.restConfig, http.MethodGet, execURL.String())
1775: +	if err != nil {
1776: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes websocket exec executor: %w", err)
1777: +	}
1778: +
1779: +	spdyExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewSPDYExecutor(r.restConfig, http.MethodPost, execURL)
1780: +	if err != nil {
1781: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes exec executor: %w", err)
1782: +	}
1783: +
1784: +	return remotecommand.NewFallbackExecutor(websocketExecutor, spdyExecutor,
1785: +		func(err error) bool {
1786: +			return streamhttp.IsUpgradeFailure(err) || streamhttp.IsHTTPSProxyError(err)
1787: +		})

1865: +	port int,

1867: +	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
1868: +	if err != nil {
1869: +		return nil, err
1870: +	}
1871: +
1872: +	if len(req.Nodes) != 1 {
1873: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("port-forward needs exactly one node, got %d", len(req.Nodes))
1874: +	}
1875: +	if port <= 0 || port > 65535 {
1876: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid port %d", port)
1877: +	}
1878: +
1879: +	location, err := r.runningNode(ctx, req.Name, req.Namespace, req.Nodes[0])
1880: +	if err != nil {
1881: +		return nil, err
1882: +	}
1883: +
1884: +	conn, err := r.dialPodPort(location.Namespace, location.Pod, port)
1885: +	if err != nil {
1886: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to port-forward to port %d of c9s node %s/%s/%s: %w",
1887: +			port, location.Namespace, req.Name, location.NodeName, err)
1888: +	}
1889: +
1890: +	return conn, nil
1891: +}
1892: +
1893: +// dialPodPort opens a forwarded connection to a pod port over SPDY. The transport is built
1894: +// from the runtime's rest config, so it carries its impersonation headers.
1895: +func (r *Runtime) dialPodPort(namespace, pod string, port int) (net.Conn, error) {
1896: +	forwardURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
1897: +		Resource("pods").
1898: +		Name(pod).
1899: +		Namespace(namespace).
1900: +		SubResource("portforward").URL()
1901: +
1902: +	transport, upgrader, err := spdy.RoundTripperFor(r.restConfig)
1903: +	if err != nil {
1904: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes port-forward transport: %w", err)
1905: +	}
1906: +
1907: +	dialer := spdy.NewDialer(upgrader, &http.Client{Transport: transport}, http.MethodPost,
1908: +		forwardURL)
1909: +
1910: +	streamConn, _, err := dialer.Dial(portforward.PortForwardProtocolV1Name)
1911: +	if err != nil {
1912: +		return nil, err
1913: +	}
1914: +
1915: +	conn, err := newPortForwardConn(streamConn, port)
1916: +	if err != nil {
1917: +		_ = streamConn.Close()
1918: +
1919: +		return nil, err
1920: +	}
1921: +
1922: +	return conn, nil
1923: +}
1924: +
1925: +// newPortForwardConn opens the error and data streams of one forwarded connection and returns
1926: +// one end of an in-memory pipe whose other end is copied to and from the data stream. The pipe
1927: +// gives the caller a complete net.Conn, deadlines included.
1928: +func newPortForwardConn(streamConn httpstream.Connection, port int) (net.Conn, error) {
1929: +	requestID := strconv.FormatInt(portForwardRequestID.Add(1), 10)
1930: +
1931: +	headers := http.Header{}
1932: +	headers.Set(corev1.StreamType, corev1.StreamTypeError)
1933: +	headers.Set(corev1.PortHeader, strconv.Itoa(port))
1934: +	headers.Set(corev1.PortForwardRequestIDHeader, requestID)
1935: +
1936: +	errorStream, err := streamConn.CreateStream(headers)
1937: +	if err != nil {
1938: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create the error stream: %w", err)
1939: +	}
1940: +	// the client sends nothing on the error stream; Close only half-closes it, so the API
1941: +	// server can still report failures on it
1942: +	_ = errorStream.Close()
1943: +
1944: +	headers.Set(corev1.StreamType, corev1.StreamTypeData)
1945: +	dataStream, err := streamConn.CreateStream(headers)
1946: +	if err != nil {
1947: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create the data stream: %w", err)
1948: +	}
1949: +
1950: +	local, remote := net.Pipe()
1951: +
1952: +	var closeOnce sync.Once
1953: +	closeAll := func() {
1954: +		closeOnce.Do(func() {
1955: +			_ = remote.Close()
1956: +			_ = dataStream.Reset()
1957: +			_ = streamConn.Close()
1958: +		})
1959: +	}
1960: +
1961: +	go func() {
1962: +		// the API server reports a failure to reach the port on the error stream
1963: +		message, _ := io.ReadAll(errorStream)
1964: +		if len(message) != 0 {
1965: +			log.Warn("Port forward failed", "port", port, "error", string(message))
1966: +			_ = remote.Close()
1967: +		}
1968: +	}()
1969: +
1970: +	go func() {
1971: +		defer closeAll()
1972: +		_, _ = io.Copy(remote, dataStream)
1973: +	}()
1974: +
1975: +	go func() {
1976: +		defer closeAll()
1977: +		_, _ = io.Copy(dataStream, remote)
1978: +	}()
1979: +
1980: +	go func() {
1981: +		<-streamConn.CloseChan()
1982: +		closeAll()
1983: +	}()
1984: +
1985: +	return local, nil
1986: +}

1988: +// SampleStats reports the CPU and memory usage of every running node of a lab from the
1989: +// resource metrics API, summing the node's device containers.
1990: +func (r *Runtime) SampleStats(
1991: +	ctx context.Context,
1992: +	req clablabruntime.InspectRequest,
1993: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, error) {
1994: +	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
1995: +	if err != nil {
1996: +		return nil, err
1997: +	}
1998: +
1999: +	state, err := r.Inspect(ctx, req)
2000: +	if err != nil {
2001: +		return nil, err
2002: +	}
2003: +
2004: +	metricsList, err := r.client.Resource(podMetricsGVR).Namespace(state.Namespace).
2005: +		List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{})
2006: +	if err != nil {
2007: +		if apierrors.IsNotFound(err) || apierrors.IsServiceUnavailable(err) ||
2008: +			apierrors.IsMethodNotSupported(err) {
2009: +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", clablabruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable, err)
2010: +		}
2011: +
2012: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read pod metrics in namespace %s: %w",
2013: +			state.Namespace, err)
2014: +	}
2015: +
2016: +	metricsByPod := make(map[string]*unstructured.Unstructured, len(metricsList.Items))
2017: +	for idx := range metricsList.Items {
2018: +		metricsByPod[metricsList.Items[idx].GetName()] = &metricsList.Items[idx]
2019: +	}
2020: +
2021: +	deviceContainers, err := r.nodeDeviceContainers(ctx, state)
2022: +	if err != nil {
2023: +		return nil, err
2024: +	}
2025: +
2026: +	stats := make([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, 0, len(state.Nodes))
2027: +	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
2028: +		podMetrics := metricsByPod[node.Pod]
2029: +		if node.Pod == "" || podMetrics == nil {
2030: +			continue
2031: +		}
2032: +
2033: +		containers := deviceContainers[node.Name]
2034: +		if len(containers) == 0 && node.Container != "" {
2035: +			containers = map[string]bool{node.Container: true}
2036: +		}
2037: +
2038: +		sample, ok := podMetricsSample(podMetrics, containers)
2039: +		if !ok {
2040: +			continue
2041: +		}
2042: +
2043: +		sample.NodeName = node.Name
2044: +		sample.Namespace = state.Namespace
2045: +		sample.Pod = node.Pod
2046: +		stats = append(stats, sample)
2047: +	}
2048: +
2049: +	return stats, nil
2050: +}

2052: +// nodeDeviceContainers reads the device containers of every node from its Node status.
2053: +func (r *Runtime) nodeDeviceContainers(
2054: +	ctx context.Context,
2055: +	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
2056: +) (map[string]map[string]bool, error) {
2057: +	nodes, err := r.nodesForTopology(ctx, state.Name, state.Namespace)
2058: +	if err != nil {
2059: +		return nil, err
2060: +	}
2061: +
2062: +	result := make(map[string]map[string]bool, len(nodes.Items))
2063: +	for idx := range nodes.Items {
2064: +		directContainers, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(
2065: +			nodes.Items[idx].Object, "status", "directContainers")
2066: +
2067: +		names := map[string]bool{}
2068: +		for _, raw := range directContainers {
2069: +			entry, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
2070: +			if !ok {
2071: +				continue
2072: +			}
2073: +			if name, _ := entry["name"].(string); name != "" {
2074: +				names[name] = true
2075: +			}
2076: +		}
2077: +		result[nodes.Items[idx].GetName()] = names
2078: +	}
2079: +
2080: +	return result, nil
2081: +}
2082: +
2083: +// podMetricsSample sums the usage of the given containers of a PodMetrics object.
2084: +func podMetricsSample(
2085: +	podMetrics *unstructured.Unstructured,
2086: +	containers map[string]bool,
2087: +) (clablabruntime.NodeStats, bool) {
2088: +	rawContainers, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(podMetrics.Object, "containers")
2089: +
2090: +	var (
2091: +		cpu    resource.Quantity
2092: +		memory resource.Quantity
2093: +		found  bool
2094: +	)
2095: +	for _, raw := range rawContainers {
2096: +		entry, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
2097: +		if !ok {
2098: +			continue
2099: +		}
2100: +		name, _ := entry["name"].(string)
2101: +		if !containers[name] {
2102: +			continue
2103: +		}
2104: +
2105: +		usage, _ := entry["usage"].(map[string]any)
2106: +		if value, ok := usage["cpu"].(string); ok {
2107: +			if quantity, err := resource.ParseQuantity(value); err == nil {
2108: +				cpu.Add(quantity)
2109: +			}
2110: +		}
2111: +		if value, ok := usage["memory"].(string); ok {
2112: +			if quantity, err := resource.ParseQuantity(value); err == nil {
2113: +				memory.Add(quantity)
2114: +			}
2115: +		}
2116: +		found = true
2117: +	}
2118: +	if !found {
2119: +		return clablabruntime.NodeStats{}, false
2120: +	}
2121: +
2122: +	sample := clablabruntime.NodeStats{
2123: +		CPUMilliCores: cpu.MilliValue(),
2124: +		MemoryBytes:   memory.Value(),
2125: +	}
2126: +	if value, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(podMetrics.Object, "timestamp"); value != "" {
2127: +		sample.Timestamp, _ = time.Parse(time.RFC3339, value)
2128: +	}
2129: +	if value, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(podMetrics.Object, "window"); value != "" {
2130: +		sample.Window, _ = time.ParseDuration(value)
2131: +	}
2132: +
2133: +	return sample, true
2134: +}

2401: +	close(resize)
2402: +	if size := queue.Next(); size != nil {
2403: +		t.Fatalf("Next() after close = %+v, want nil", size)
2404: +	}
2405: +
2406: +	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
2407: +	cancel()
2408: +	if size := newTerminalSizeQueue(
2409: +		ctx,
2410: +		make(chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize),
2411: +	).Next(); size != nil {
2412: +		t.Fatalf("Next() after cancel = %+v, want nil", size)
2413: +	}
2414: +}
2415: +
2416: +// impersonationRecorder is an API server stub that records the impersonation headers of every
2417: +// request and answers with a Status error.
2418: +type impersonationRecorder struct {
2419: +	mu       sync.Mutex
2420: +	requests []recordedRequest
2421: +}
2422: +
2423: +type recordedRequest struct {
2424: +	method string
2425: +	path   string
2426: +	user   string
2427: +	groups []string
2428: +}
2429: +
2430: +func (rec *impersonationRecorder) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
2431: +	rec.mu.Lock()
2432: +	rec.requests = append(rec.requests, recordedRequest{
2433: +		method: req.Method,
2434: +		path:   req.URL.Path,
2435: +		user:   req.Header.Get("Impersonate-User"),
2436: +		groups: req.Header.Values("Impersonate-Group"),
2437: +	})
2438: +	rec.mu.Unlock()
2439: +
2440: +	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
2441: +	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusForbidden)
2442: +	_, _ = io.WriteString(w,
2443: +		`{"kind":"Status","apiVersion":"v1","status":"Failure","reason":"Forbidden","code":403}`)
2444: +}
2445: +
2446: +func (rec *impersonationRecorder) take() []recordedRequest {
2447: +	rec.mu.Lock()
2448: +	defer rec.mu.Unlock()
2449: +
2450: +	requests := rec.requests
2451: +	rec.requests = nil
2452: +
2453: +	return requests
2454: +}
2455: +
2456: +func TestIdentityImpersonatesOnEveryTransport(t *testing.T) {
2457: +	t.Parallel()
2458: +
2459: +	recorder := &impersonationRecorder{}
2460: +	server := httptest.NewServer(recorder)
2461: +	defer server.Close()
2462: +
2463: +	r := &Runtime{
2464: +		identity: clablabruntime.Identity{User: "clab:default"},
2465: +		clients: &clientLoader{
2466: +			loadConfig: func() (*rest.Config, string, error) {
2467: +				return &rest.Config{Host: server.URL}, "", nil
2468: +			},
2469: +			newClients: newKubeClients,
2470: +		},
2471: +	}
2472: +	alice := clablabruntime.Identity{
2473: +		User:   "clab:alice",
2474: +		Groups: []string{"clab:users", "clab:admins"},
2475: +	}
2476: +
2477: +	view, err := r.connect(alice)
2478: +	if err != nil {
2479: +		t.Fatal(err)
2480: +	}
2481: +	again, err := r.connect(alice)
2482: +	if err != nil || again.kubeClient != view.kubeClient {
2483: +		t.Fatal("clients of one identity were not cached")
2484: +	}
2485: +	defaultView, err := r.connect(clablabruntime.Identity{})
2486: +	if err != nil || defaultView.kubeClient == view.kubeClient {
2487: +		t.Fatal("the configured identity shares the clients of another identity")
2488: +	}
2489: +
2490: +	ctx := context.Background()
2491: +	pod := &corev1.Pod{ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Name: "lab1-r1-abc", Namespace: "lab-ns"}}
2492: +
2493: +	// REST
2494: +	_, _ = r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1", Identity: alice})
2495: +	// pod exec: websocket first, then SPDY
2496: +	_, _, _, _ = view.execInPod(ctx, pod, "node-r1-x", []string{"true"})
2497: +	// port-forward over SPDY
2498: +	if conn, err := view.dialPodPort("lab-ns", "lab1-r1-abc", 22); err == nil {
2499: +		_ = conn.Close()
2500: +	}
2501: +	// a call without identity uses the configured one
2502: +	_, _ = r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1"})
2503: +
2504: +	requests := recorder.take()
2505: +	seen := map[string]bool{}
2506: +	for _, req := range requests {
2507: +		switch {
2508: +		case strings.HasSuffix(req.path, "/exec"):
2509: +			seen["exec-"+req.method] = true
2510: +		case strings.HasSuffix(req.path, "/portforward"):
2511: +			seen["portforward"] = true
2512: +		default:
2513: +			seen["rest-"+req.user] = true
2514: +		}
2515: +
2516: +		if req.user == "clab:default" {
2517: +			if len(req.groups) != 0 {
2518: +				t.Fatalf("configured identity sent groups: %+v", req)
2519: +			}
2520: +			continue
2521: +		}
2522: +		if req.user != alice.User || strings.Join(req.groups, ",") != "clab:users,clab:admins" {
2523: +			t.Fatalf("request without alice's impersonation: %+v", req)
2524: +		}
2525: +	}
2526: +
2527: +	for _, want := range []string{
2528: +		"rest-clab:alice", "exec-GET", "exec-POST", "portforward", "rest-clab:default",
2529: +	} {
2530: +		if !seen[want] {
2531: +			t.Fatalf("no %s request recorded: %+v", want, requests)
2532: +		}
2533: +	}
2534: +}

The user gets connection reset instead of an informative error. Acceptable design; skip or coverage note.

55. **`DialPort` validation `port <= 0 || port > 65535`** — OK.

56. **`cmd/logs.go` tail flag Int64** — `--tail` negative default -1 means whole log; docs match. But `--tail 0` shows no lines. In core NodeLogs: `if o.Logs.Tail >= 0 { tail := o.Logs.Tail; opts.Tail = &tail }`. So tail=0 → &0 → LogTail → "0". Docker with Tail "0" → no lines. OK. But `--tail -5`? Tail=-5 <0 → whole log. Slight: `--tail -5` treated as whole log rather than error. Docs say default -1 shows whole log; negative behaves as whole. Fine.

57. **`inspect` in `LocateNode`** — uses state from Inspect; Inspect errors if lab not found. OK.

58. **Check `requireLabName` before `labRuntimeCapability` in LocateLabRuntimeNodes** order — capability first then lab name; error message ordering. Fine.

The diff hunk shows the condition chain where each `cobraCmd.Name() != "X"` — the added `!= "logs"` means logs now falls through (doesn't return nil early). Good.

62. **Robot test in 01-linux-lifecycle.robot**: `logs -t ${topo} -n client` — uses Run Clab Command keyword. And the library test runs `go test ./core/ -run TestC9sClusterNodeAccess` — the test requires "client" node with port 80 HTTP. Presumably matching earlier topology. Also `Should Not Contain ${result.stdout} SKIP` — if go test prints "SKIP" anywhere... e.g., subtests skipped. It asserts no SKIP. OK.

46: // LocateNode reports the pod, primary device container, Node UID and exposed ports of the

49: func (r *Runtime) LocateNode(
50: 	ctx context.Context,
51: 	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
52: ) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
53: 	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
54: 	if err != nil {
55: 		return nil, err
56: 	}
57: 
58: 	state, err := r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
59: 		Name:      req.Name,
60: 		Namespace: req.Namespace,
61: 	})
62: 	if err != nil {
63: 		return nil, err
64: 	}
65: 
66: 	nodes := make(map[string]clablabruntime.NodeState, len(state.Nodes))
67: 	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
68: 		nodes[node.Name] = node
69: 	}
70: 
71: 	if len(req.Nodes) == 0 {
72: 		locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(state.Nodes))
73: 		for _, node := range state.Nodes {
74: 			locations = append(locations, nodeLocation(state, node))
75: 		}
76: 
77: 		return locations, nil
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(req.Nodes))
81: 	for _, nodeName := range req.Nodes {
82: 		resolved, ok := resolveKnownNodeName(nodes, nodeName)
83: 		if !ok {
84: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("node %q was not found in c9s lab %s/%s",
85: 				nodeName, state.Namespace, state.Name)
86: 		}
87: 		locations = append(locations, nodeLocation(state, nodes[resolved]))
88: 	}
89: 
90: 	return locations, nil
91: }

216: // newExecutor streams a pod exec over websockets, falling back to SPDY when the API server
217: // does not upgrade the websocket, like kubectl. The websocket executor reports upgrade
218: // failures with the k8s.io/streaming error types. Both transports are built from the runtime's
219: // rest config, so they carry its impersonation headers.
220: func (r *Runtime) newExecutor(execURL *url.URL) (remotecommand.Executor, error) {
221: 	websocketExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewWebSocketExecutor(
222: 		r.restConfig, http.MethodGet, execURL.String())
223: 	if err != nil {
224: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes websocket exec executor: %w", err)
225: 	}
226: 
227: 	spdyExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewSPDYExecutor(r.restConfig, http.MethodPost, execURL)
228: 	if err != nil {
229: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes exec executor: %w", err)
230: 	}
231: 
232: 	return remotecommand.NewFallbackExecutor(websocketExecutor, spdyExecutor,
233: 		func(err error) bool {
234: 			return streamhttp.IsUpgradeFailure(err) || streamhttp.IsHTTPSProxyError(err)
235: 		})
236: }

238: // terminalSizeQueue adapts a resize channel to the remotecommand size queue.
239: type terminalSizeQueue struct {
240: 	ctx    context.Context
241: 	resize <-chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize
242: }
243: 
244: func newTerminalSizeQueue(
245: 	ctx context.Context,
246: 	resize <-chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize,
247: ) *terminalSizeQueue {
248: 	return &terminalSizeQueue{ctx: ctx, resize: resize}
249: }

251: // Next blocks until the next size change; nil ends resizing.
252: func (q *terminalSizeQueue) Next() *remotecommand.TerminalSize {
253: 	select {
254: 	case <-q.ctx.Done():
255: 		return nil
256: 	case size, ok := <-q.resize:
257: 		if !ok {
258: 			return nil
259: 		}
260: 
261: 		return &remotecommand.TerminalSize{Width: size.Width, Height: size.Height}
262: 	}
263: }

308: // DialPort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node's pod through the Kubernetes port-forward
309: // subresource.
310: func (r *Runtime) DialPort(
311: 	ctx context.Context,
312: 	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
313: 	port int,
314: ) (net.Conn, error) {
315: 	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
316: 	if err != nil {
317: 		return nil, err
318: 	}
319: 
320: 	if len(req.Nodes) != 1 {
321: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("port-forward needs exactly one node, got %d", len(req.Nodes))
322: 	}
323: 	if port <= 0 || port > 65535 {
324: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid port %d", port)
325: 	}
326: 
327: 	location, err := r.runningNode(ctx, req.Name, req.Namespace, req.Nodes[0])
328: 	if err != nil {
329: 		return nil, err
330: 	}
331: 
332: 	conn, err := r.dialPodPort(location.Namespace, location.Pod, port)
333: 	if err != nil {
334: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to port-forward to port %d of c9s node %s/%s/%s: %w",
335: 			port, location.Namespace, req.Name, location.NodeName, err)
336: 	}
337: 
338: 	return conn, nil
339: }

341: // dialPodPort opens a forwarded connection to a pod port over SPDY. The transport is built
342: // from the runtime's rest config, so it carries its impersonation headers.
343: func (r *Runtime) dialPodPort(namespace, pod string, port int) (net.Conn, error) {
344: 	forwardURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
345: 		Resource("pods").
346: 		Name(pod).
347: 		Namespace(namespace).
348: 		SubResource("portforward").URL()
349: 
350: 	transport, upgrader, err := spdy.RoundTripperFor(r.restConfig)
351: 	if err != nil {
352: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes port-forward transport: %w", err)
353: 	}
354: 
355: 	dialer := spdy.NewDialer(upgrader, &http.Client{Transport: transport}, http.MethodPost,
356: 		forwardURL)
357: 
358: 	streamConn, _, err := dialer.Dial(portforward.PortForwardProtocolV1Name)
359: 	if err != nil {
360: 		return nil, err
361: 	}
362: 
363: 	conn, err := newPortForwardConn(streamConn, port)
364: 	if err != nil {
365: 		_ = streamConn.Close()
366: 
367: 		return nil, err
368: 	}
369: 
370: 	return conn, nil
371: }
372: 
373: // newPortForwardConn opens the error and data streams of one forwarded connection and returns
374: // one end of an in-memory pipe whose other end is copied to and from the data stream. The pipe
375: // gives the caller a complete net.Conn, deadlines included.
376: func newPortForwardConn(streamConn httpstream.Connection, port int) (net.Conn, error) {
377: 	requestID := strconv.FormatInt(portForwardRequestID.Add(1), 10)
378: 
379: 	headers := http.Header{}
380: 	headers.Set(corev1.StreamType, corev1.StreamTypeError)
381: 	headers.Set(corev1.PortHeader, strconv.Itoa(port))
382: 	headers.Set(corev1.PortForwardRequestIDHeader, requestID)
383: 
384: 	errorStream, err := streamConn.CreateStream(headers)
385: 	if err != nil {
386: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create the error stream: %w", err)
387: 	}
388: 	// the client sends nothing on the error stream; Close only half-closes it, so the API
389: 	// server can still report failures on it
390: 	_ = errorStream.Close()
391: 
392: 	headers.Set(corev1.StreamType, corev1.StreamTypeData)
393: 	dataStream, err := streamConn.CreateStream(headers)
394: 	if err != nil {
395: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create the data stream: %w", err)
396: 	}
397: 
398: 	local, remote := net.Pipe()
399: 
400: 	var closeOnce sync.Once
401: 	closeAll := func() {
402: 		closeOnce.Do(func() {
403: 			_ = remote.Close()
404: 			_ = dataStream.Reset()
405: 			_ = streamConn.Close()
406: 		})
407: 	}
408: 
409: 	go func() {
410: 		// the API server reports a failure to reach the port on the error stream
411: 		message, _ := io.ReadAll(errorStream)
412: 		if len(message) != 0 {
413: 			log.Warn("Port forward failed", "port", port, "error", string(message))
414: 			_ = remote.Close()
415: 		}
416: 	}()
417: 
418: 	go func() {
419: 		defer closeAll()
420: 		_, _ = io.Copy(remote, dataStream)
421: 	}()
422: 
423: 	go func() {
424: 		defer closeAll()
425: 		_, _ = io.Copy(dataStream, remote)
426: 	}()
427: 
428: 	go func() {
429: 		<-streamConn.CloseChan()
430: 		closeAll()
431: 	}()
432: 
433: 	return local, nil
434: }

436: // SampleStats reports the CPU and memory usage of every running node of a lab from the
437: // resource metrics API, summing the node's device containers.
438: func (r *Runtime) SampleStats(
439: 	ctx context.Context,
440: 	req clablabruntime.InspectRequest,
441: ) ([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, error) {
442: 	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
443: 	if err != nil {
444: 		return nil, err
445: 	}
446: 
447: 	state, err := r.Inspect(ctx, req)
448: 	if err != nil {
449: 		return nil, err
450: 	}
451: 
452: 	metricsList, err := r.client.Resource(podMetricsGVR).Namespace(state.Namespace).
453: 		List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{})
454: 	if err != nil {
455: 		if apierrors.IsNotFound(err) || apierrors.IsServiceUnavailable(err) ||
456: 			apierrors.IsMethodNotSupported(err) {
457: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", clablabruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable, err)
458: 		}
459: 
460: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read pod metrics in namespace %s: %w",
461: 			state.Namespace, err)
462: 	}
463: 
464: 	metricsByPod := make(map[string]*unstructured.Unstructured, len(metricsList.Items))
465: 	for idx := range metricsList.Items {
466: 		metricsByPod[metricsList.Items[idx].GetName()] = &metricsList.Items[idx]
467: 	}
468: 
469: 	deviceContainers, err := r.nodeDeviceContainers(ctx, state)
470: 	if err != nil {
471: 		return nil, err
472: 	}
473: 
474: 	stats := make([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, 0, len(state.Nodes))
475: 	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
476: 		podMetrics := metricsByPod[node.Pod]
477: 		if node.Pod == "" || podMetrics == nil {
478: 			continue
479: 		}
480: 
481: 		containers := deviceContainers[node.Name]
482: 		if len(containers) == 0 && node.Container != "" {
483: 			containers = map[string]bool{node.Container: true}
484: 		}
485: 
486: 		sample, ok := podMetricsSample(podMetrics, containers)
487: 		if !ok {
488: 			continue
489: 		}
490: 
491: 		sample.NodeName = node.Name
492: 		sample.Namespace = state.Namespace
493: 		sample.Pod = node.Pod
494: 		stats = append(stats, sample)
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	return stats, nil
498: }

500: // nodeDeviceContainers reads the device containers of every node from its Node status.
501: func (r *Runtime) nodeDeviceContainers(
502: 	ctx context.Context,
503: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
504: ) (map[string]map[string]bool, error) {
505: 	nodes, err := r.nodesForTopology(ctx, state.Name, state.Namespace)
506: 	if err != nil {
507: 		return nil, err
508: 	}
509: 
510: 	result := make(map[string]map[string]bool, len(nodes.Items))
511: 	for idx := range nodes.Items {
512: 		directContainers, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(
513: 			nodes.Items[idx].Object, "status", "directContainers")
514: 
515: 		names := map[string]bool{}
516: 		for _, raw := range directContainers {
517: 			entry, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
518: 			if !ok {
519: 				continue
520: 			}
521: 			if name, _ := entry["name"].(string); name != "" {
522: 				names[name] = true
523: 			}
524: 		}
525: 		result[nodes.Items[idx].GetName()] = names
526: 	}
527: 
528: 	return result, nil
529: }
530: 
531: // podMetricsSample sums the usage of the given containers of a PodMetrics object.
532: func podMetricsSample(
533: 	podMetrics *unstructured.Unstructured,
534: 	containers map[string]bool,
535: ) (clablabruntime.NodeStats, bool) {
536: 	rawContainers, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(podMetrics.Object, "containers")
537: 
538: 	var (
539: 		cpu    resource.Quantity
540: 		memory resource.Quantity
541: 		found  bool
542: 	)
543: 	for _, raw := range rawContainers {
544: 		entry, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
545: 		if !ok {
546: 			continue
547: 		}
548: 		name, _ := entry["name"].(string)
549: 		if !containers[name] {
550: 			continue
551: 		}
552: 
553: 		usage, _ := entry["usage"].(map[string]any)
554: 		if value, ok := usage["cpu"].(string); ok {
555: 			if quantity, err := resource.ParseQuantity(value); err == nil {
556: 				cpu.Add(quantity)
557: 			}
558: 		}
559: 		if value, ok := usage["memory"].(string); ok {
560: 			if quantity, err := resource.ParseQuantity(value); err == nil {
561: 				memory.Add(quantity)
562: 			}
563: 		}
564: 		found = true
565: 	}
566: 	if !found {
567: 		return clablabruntime.NodeStats{}, false
568: 	}
569: 
570: 	sample := clablabruntime.NodeStats{
571: 		CPUMilliCores: cpu.MilliValue(),
572: 		MemoryBytes:   memory.Value(),
573: 	}
574: 	if value, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(podMetrics.Object, "timestamp"); value != "" {
575: 		sample.Timestamp, _ = time.Parse(time.RFC3339, value)
576: 	}
577: 	if value, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(podMetrics.Object, "window"); value != "" {
578: 		sample.Window, _ = time.ParseDuration(value)
579: 	}
580: 
581: 	return sample, true
582: }

Reasoning
Podman issue analysis: in the normal path (`case err := <-done: return nil`), the goroutine `done <- containers.Logs(...)` sent into buffered done; the main consumed it. After that, if the podman binding sender is still sending on stdoutCh/stderrCh (it sends without watching ctx per comment), the main loop has returned, so no reader → the internal podman goroutine blocks forever → goroutine leak. But does containers.Logs return only after finishing all sends? Per the comment, "the bindings send on the channels without watching the context; keep draining them after an early return so the sender can finish". The "early return" is the write-error path. What about the normal `done` path? containers.Logs should only return after it stopped sending... presumably. Actually if Logs(ctx...) gets ctx canceled, it returns an error without draining its own pending sends? The comment suggests sends happen in goroutines inside the podman library. If Logs returns due to ctx cancel while its internal goroutines still try to send on stdoutCh/stderrCh, those internal sends block forever → leak inside podman library, not ours. This is speculative. But note the comment says "keep draining them after an early return so the sender can finish" — only covers the write-error path. The done path may also have pending sends. Hmm — the comment says "after an early return" — maybe done-path is not an early return. I'll treat as coverage note.

Actually there's a more concrete race: main select has three cases; suppose io.WriteString fails on stdout, calls drain() (spawns goroutine), returns err. Then the podman goroutine eventually sends done; drain consumes done and exits. Fine. But there's also the case where both stdout and stderr write fail concurrently? Only one select iteration at a time. Fine.

One more potential podman race: in the write-error path, drain() is reading stdoutCh/stderrCh; suppose the sender goroutine is blocked sending on stderrCh while main loop is also blocked... no, main returned.

OK. Now potential real bug: in the normal path, if `done` has `err != nil` but `ctx.Err() == nil`, returns wrapped err — fine. If follow mode with follow=true and the caller's ctx is canceled — podman binding may return a ctx error → wrapped only if ctx.Err()==nil. Fine.

Next: check `runtime/runtime.go` LogTail and interface; check `core` NodeLogs/NodeAccess plumbing; check `core/runtime_state.go` and `core/events/stream.go` and `cmd/labruntime_gaps_test.go`. Also check tests: 31*.robot existence; 14-clabernetes robot file variables (events-log, events-err); smoke robot 32-logs.robot.

1: package core

3: import (

13: 	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"

16: // The helpers in this file give library users per-node access to the lab selected by the CLab
17: // (its topology file or WithTopologyName). Node names are accepted as the topology file spells
18: // them or as a lab runtime sanitized them. Lab runtime calls act as the identity set with
19: // WithLabRuntimeIdentity.
20: 
21: // LocateLabRuntimeNodes reports the workload (namespace, pod, primary device container, Node
22: // UID, exposed ports) of the given nodes, or of every node of the lab when none are given.
23: func (c *CLab) LocateLabRuntimeNodes(
24: 	ctx context.Context,
25: 	nodeNames ...string,
26: ) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
27: 	locator, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLocator](c, "locating nodes")
28: 	if err != nil {
29: 		return nil, err
30: 	}
31: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
32: 		return nil, err
33: 	}
34: 
35: 	return locator.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
36: 		Name:     c.Config.Name,
37: 		Nodes:    nodeNames,
38: 		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
39: 	})
40: }
41: 
42: // AttachLabRuntimeNode runs an interactive command in a node's device container (or in
43: // req.Container) with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing. The lab name and identity
44: // default to the CLab's. A command exiting nonzero returns a *labruntime.CommandExitError.
45: func (c *CLab) AttachLabRuntimeNode(
46: 	ctx context.Context,
47: 	req clablabruntime.AttachRequest,
48: 	streams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,
49: ) error {
50: 	attacher, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeAttacher](c, "attaching to nodes")
51: 	if err != nil {
52: 		return err
53: 	}
54: 
55: 	if req.Name == "" {
56: 		if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
57: 			return err
58: 		}
59: 		req.Name = c.Config.Name
60: 	}
61: 	if req.Identity.IsZero() {
62: 		req.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity
63: 	}
64: 
65: 	return attacher.Attach(ctx, req, streams)
66: }
67: 
68: // DialLabRuntimeNodePort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node (SSH, web UIs) through the
69: // lab runtime, such as a Kubernetes port-forward.
70: func (c *CLab) DialLabRuntimeNodePort(
71: 	ctx context.Context,
72: 	nodeName string,
73: 	port int,
74: ) (net.Conn, error) {
75: 	forwarder, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodePortForwarder](
76: 		c, "port-forwarding to nodes")
77: 	if err != nil {
78: 		return nil, err
79: 	}
80: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
81: 		return nil, err
82: 	}
83: 
84: 	return forwarder.DialPort(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
85: 		Name:     c.Config.Name,
86: 		Nodes:    []string{nodeName},
87: 		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
88: 	}, port)
89: }
90: 
91: // SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats reports the CPU and memory usage of the lab's running nodes. It
92: // returns an error wrapping labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable when the cluster serves no resource
93: // metrics.
94: func (c *CLab) SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats(ctx context.Context) ([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, error) {
95: 	sampler, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeStatsSampler](
96: 		c, "sampling node stats")
97: 	if err != nil {
98: 		return nil, err
99: 	}
100: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
101: 		return nil, err
102: 	}
103: 
104: 	return sampler.SampleStats(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
105: 		Name:     c.Config.Name,
106: 		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
107: 	})
108: }
109: 
110: // NodeLogOptions selects the node log NodeLogs writes.
111: type NodeLogOptions struct {
112: 	// NodeName is the node whose log is written.
113: 	NodeName string
114: 	// Container overrides a lab runtime node's primary device container. Local runtimes do
115: 	// not support it.
116: 	Container string
117: 	// Tail limits the output to the last lines of the log; nil writes the whole log.
118: 	Tail *int64
119: 	// Follow keeps writing new log lines until the context ends.
120: 	Follow bool
121: 	// Timestamps prefixes every line with its timestamp.
122: 	Timestamps bool
123: }
124: 
125: // NodeLogs writes the log of a lab node with every runtime: the container log with Docker and
126: // Podman, the device container log with a lab runtime. Lab runtimes write one combined stream to
127: // stdout.
128: func (c *CLab) NodeLogs(
129: 	ctx context.Context,
130: 	opts NodeLogOptions,
131: 	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
132: ) error {
133: 	if opts.NodeName == "" {
134: 		return fmt.Errorf("node name is required")
135: 	}
136: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
137: 		return err
138: 	}
139: 
140: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
141: 		streamer, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLogStreamer](
142: 			c, "streaming node logs")
143: 		if err != nil {
144: 			return err
145: 		}
146: 
147: 		return streamer.StreamLogs(ctx, clablabruntime.LogRequest{
148: 			Name:       c.Config.Name,
149: 			NodeName:   opts.NodeName,
150: 			Container:  opts.Container,
151: 			Tail:       opts.Tail,
152: 			Follow:     opts.Follow,
153: 			Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
154: 			Identity:   c.labRuntimeIdentity,
155: 		}, stdout)
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	if opts.Container != "" {
159: 		return fmt.Errorf("selecting a container is only supported with lab runtimes")
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	runtime, containerName, err := c.nodeContainer(ctx, opts.NodeName)
163: 	if err != nil {
164: 		return err
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	writer, ok := runtime.(clabruntime.ContainerLogWriter)
168: 	if !ok {
169: 		return fmt.Errorf("container runtime %q does not support node logs", runtime.GetName())
170: 	}
171: 
172: 	return writer.WriteContainerLogs(ctx, containerName, clabruntime.ContainerLogOptions{
173: 		Tail:       opts.Tail,
174: 		Follow:     opts.Follow,
175: 		Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
176: 	}, stdout, stderr)
177: }
178: 
179: // nodeContainer finds the container of a lab node in the local container runtimes by the lab
180: // and node name labels.
181: func (c *CLab) nodeContainer(
182: 	ctx context.Context,
183: 	nodeName string,
184: ) (clabruntime.ContainerRuntime, string, error) {
185: 	filters := []*clabtypes.GenericFilter{
186: 		{
187: 			FilterType: "label",
188: 			Field:      clabconstants.Containerlab,
189: 			Operator:   "=",
190: 			Match:      c.Config.Name,
191: 		},
192: 		{
193: 			FilterType: "label",
194: 			Field:      clabconstants.NodeName,
195: 			Operator:   "=",
196: 			Match:      nodeName,
197: 		},
198: 	}
199: 
200: 	runtimeNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Runtimes))
201: 	for name := range c.Runtimes {
202: 		runtimeNames = append(runtimeNames, name)
203: 	}
204: 	sort.Strings(runtimeNames)
205: 
206: 	for _, name := range runtimeNames {
207: 		runtime := c.Runtimes[name]
208: 
209: 		containers, err := runtime.ListContainers(ctx, filters)
210: 		if err != nil {
211: 			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("could not list containers: %w", err)
212: 		}
213: 		if len(containers) != 0 && len(containers[0].Names) != 0 {
214: 			return runtime, containers[0].Names[0], nil
215: 		}
216: 	}
217: 
218: 	return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: node %q of lab %q has no container",
219: 		ErrNodeNotFound, nodeName, c.Config.Name)
220: }
221: 
222: func (c *CLab) requireLabName() error {
223: 	if c.Config == nil || c.Config.Name == "" {
224: 		return fmt.Errorf("provide a lab name (--name) or a topology file (--topo)")
225: 	}
226: 
227: 	return nil
228: }
229: 
230: // labRuntimeCapability returns the CLab's lab runtime as an optional lab runtime interface.
231: func labRuntimeCapability[T any](c *CLab, operation string) (T, error) {
232: 	var zero T
233: 
234: 	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
235: 		return zero, fmt.Errorf("%s needs a lab runtime such as %q",
236: 			operation, clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName)
237: 	}
238: 
239: 	capability, ok := c.LabRuntime.(T)
240: 	if !ok {
241: 		return zero, fmt.Errorf("lab runtime %q does not support %s",
242: 			c.globalRuntimeName, operation)
243: 	}
244: 
245: 	return capability, nil
246: }
