Let me check `NewContainerLab` and `WithTopoPath`. Save command also doesn't call ParseTopo — `c.Save` probably parses. Check core: does Save call ParseTopo? Let me check how Save gets the lab name.

328: 		namespace, labName, nodeName, err := labRuntimeContainerParts(containers[idx])
329: 		if err != nil {
330: 			log.Warnf("exec target %s is invalid: %v", containers[idx].Names[0], err)
331: 			execErrors = append(execErrors, fmt.Errorf(
332: 				"exec target %s is invalid: %w", containers[idx].Names[0], err))
333: 			continue
334: 		}
335: 
336: 		for _, execCmd := range execCmds {
337: 			result, err := c.LabRuntime.Exec(ctx, clablabruntime.ExecRequest{
338: 				Identity:  c.labRuntimeIdentity,
339: 				Name:      labName,
340: 				Namespace: namespace,
341: 				NodeName:  nodeName,
342: 				Command:   execCmd.GetCmd(),
343: 			})
344: 			if err != nil {
345: 				log.Warnf("exec on %s failed: %v", containers[idx].Names[0], err)
346: 				execErrors = append(execErrors, fmt.Errorf(
347: 					"exec on %s failed: %w", containers[idx].Names[0], err))
348: 				continue
349: 			}
350: 
351: 			resultCollection.Add(containers[idx].Names[0], result)
352: 			if result.GetReturnCode() != 0 {
353: 				execErrors = append(execErrors, fmt.Errorf(
354: 					"exec on %s returned exit code %d",
355: 					containers[idx].Names[0],
356: 					result.GetReturnCode(),
357: 				))
358: 			}
359: 		}
360: 	}
361: 
362: 	return resultCollection, errors.Join(execErrors...)
363: }

418: func (c *CLab) containersFromLabState(
419: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
420: ) []clabruntime.GenericContainer {
421: 	if state == nil {
422: 		return nil
423: 	}
424: 
425: 	nodes := state.Nodes
426: 	if len(nodes) == 0 && c.Config.Topology != nil {
427: 		nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Config.Topology.Nodes))
428: 		for nodeName := range c.Config.Topology.Nodes {
429: 			nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
430: 		}
431: 		sort.Strings(nodeNames)
432: 
433: 		nodes = make([]clablabruntime.NodeState, 0, len(nodeNames))
434: 		for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
435: 			nodes = append(nodes, clablabruntime.NodeState{
436: 				Name:  nodeName,
437: 				Kind:  c.Config.Topology.GetNodeKind(nodeName),
438: 				Image: c.Config.Topology.GetNodeImage(nodeName),
439: 				State: state.State,
440: 				Ready: state.Ready,
441: 			})
442: 		}
443: 	}
444: 
445: 	containers := make([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, 0, len(nodes))
446: 	for _, node := range nodes {
447: 		containers = append(containers, c.containerFromLabNode(state, node))
448: 	}
449: 
450: 	return containers
451: }

453: func (c *CLab) containerFromLabNode(
454: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
455: 	node clablabruntime.NodeState,
456: ) clabruntime.GenericContainer {
457: 	nodeName := fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", state.Name, node.Name)
458: 	containerState := node.State
459: 	containerStatus := node.State
460: 	if containerState == "" {
461: 		containerState = state.State
462: 	}
463: 	if node.Ready {
464: 		containerState = "running"
465: 		containerStatus = "healthy"
466: 	}
467: 
468: 	labels := map[string]string{
469: 		clabconstants.Containerlab: state.Name,
470: 		clabconstants.NodeName:     node.Name,
471: 		clabconstants.LongName:     nodeName,
472: 		clabconstants.TopoFile:     labRuntimeTopologyPath(c, state),
473: 	}
474: 
475: 	var image string
476: 	if c.Config.Topology != nil {
477: 		topologyNode := c.topologyNodeName(node.Name)
478: 		labels[clabconstants.NodeKind] = c.Config.Topology.GetNodeKind(topologyNode)
479: 		image = c.Config.Topology.GetNodeImage(topologyNode)
480: 
481: 		if group := c.Config.Topology.GetNodeGroup(topologyNode); group != "" {
482: 			labels[clabconstants.NodeGroup] = group
483: 		}
484: 	}
485: 	if node.Kind != "" {
486: 		labels[clabconstants.NodeKind] = node.Kind
487: 	}
488: 	if node.Image != "" {
489: 		image = node.Image
490: 	}
491: 
492: 	if state.Owner != "" {
493: 		labels[clabconstants.Owner] = state.Owner
494: 	} else if c.customOwner != "" {
495: 		labels[clabconstants.Owner] = c.customOwner
496: 	}
497: 
498: 	// The ID names the node uniquely across namespaces and labs. It is also the short ID, so
499: 	// inspect reports it as container_id and it matches the events actor ID.
500: 	id := labRuntimeContainerID(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name)
501: 
502: 	return clabruntime.GenericContainer{
503: 		Names:           []string{nodeName},
504: 		ID:              id,
505: 		ShortID:         id,
506: 		Image:           image,
507: 		State:           containerState,
508: 		Status:          containerStatus,
509: 		Labels:          labels,
510: 		NetworkName:     state.Namespace,
511: 		NetworkSettings: managementAddress(node),
512: 		Workload: &clabtypes.LabRuntimeWorkload{
513: 			Namespace:           state.Namespace,
514: 			Pod:                 node.Pod,
515: 			Container:           node.Container,
516: 			NodeUID:             node.NodeUID,
517: 			ExposedPorts:        node.ExposedPorts,
518: 			LoadBalancerAddress: node.LoadBalancerAddress,
519: 		},
520: 	}
521: }
522: 
523: // labRuntimeContainerID is the ID of a lab runtime node: <namespace>/<lab>/<node>.
524: func labRuntimeContainerID(namespace, lab, node string) string {
525: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/%s", namespace, lab, node)
526: }
527: 
528: // topologyNodeName maps a node name a lab runtime reports back onto the topology node it belongs
529: // to. The runtime renames the nodes Kubernetes cannot carry, so the state it reports does not
530: // always use the name the topology file wrote.
531: func (c *CLab) topologyNodeName(name string) string {
532: 	if c.Config.Topology == nil {
533: 		return name
534: 	}
535: 	if _, ok := c.Config.Topology.Nodes[name]; ok {
536: 		return name
537: 	}
538: 
539: 	for nodeName := range c.Config.Topology.Nodes {
540: 		if clabnames.SanitizeName(nodeName) == name {
541: 			return nodeName
542: 		}
543: 	}
544: 
545: 	return name
546: }
547: 
548: // managementAddress reports the address a user reaches the node at: the LoadBalancer address
549: // when the node is exposed, otherwise the allocated management address.
550: func managementAddress(node clablabruntime.NodeState) clabruntime.GenericMgmtIPs {
551: 	settings := clabruntime.GenericMgmtIPs{}
552: 
553: 	if ip := net.ParseIP(node.LoadBalancerAddress); ip != nil {
554: 		if ip.To4() != nil {
555: 			settings.IPv4addr = node.LoadBalancerAddress
556: 			settings.IPv4pLen = 32
557: 		} else {
558: 			settings.IPv6addr = node.LoadBalancerAddress
559: 			settings.IPv6pLen = 128
560: 		}
561: 	}
562: 
563: 	if settings.IPv4addr == "" {
564: 		settings.IPv4addr, settings.IPv4pLen = splitManagementCIDR(node.MgmtIPv4Address)
565: 	}
566: 	if settings.IPv6addr == "" {
567: 		settings.IPv6addr, settings.IPv6pLen = splitManagementCIDR(node.MgmtIPv6Address)
568: 	}
569: 
570: 	return settings
571: }
572: 
573: func splitManagementCIDR(cidr string) (string, int) {
574: 	if cidr == "" {
575: 		return "", 0
576: 	}
577: 
578: 	ip, network, err := net.ParseCIDR(cidr)
579: 	if err != nil {
580: 		if net.ParseIP(cidr) != nil {
581: 			return cidr, 0
582: 		}
583: 
584: 		return "", 0
585: 	}
586: 
587: 	prefixLen, _ := network.Mask.Size()
588: 
589: 	return ip.String(), prefixLen
590: }

592: func labRuntimeTopologyPath(c *CLab, state *clablabruntime.LabState) string {
593: 	if c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileIsSet() {
594: 		return c.TopoPaths.TopologyFilenameAbsPath()
595: 	}
596: 
597: 	if state.TopologyPath != "" {

599: 	}
600: 
601: 	return fmt.Sprintf("k8s://%s/topologies/%s", state.Namespace, state.Name)

604: func labRuntimeContainerParts(c clabruntime.GenericContainer) (string, string, string, error) {
605: 	parts := strings.Split(c.ID, "/")
606: 	if len(parts) != 3 {
607: 		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("expected namespace/lab/node id, got %q", c.ID)
608: 	}
609: 
610: 	return parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], nil
611: }

613: func filterLabRuntimeContainers(
614: 	containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,
615: 	filters []*clabtypes.GenericFilter,
616: ) []clabruntime.GenericContainer {
617: 	if len(filters) == 0 {
618: 		return containers
619: 	}
620: 
621: 	filtered := make([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, 0, len(containers))
622: 	for _, container := range containers {
623: 		if labRuntimeContainerMatches(container, filters) {
624: 			filtered = append(filtered, container)
625: 		}
626: 	}
627: 
628: 	return filtered
629: }
630: 
631: func labRuntimeContainerMatches(
632: 	container clabruntime.GenericContainer,
633: 	filters []*clabtypes.GenericFilter,
634: ) bool {
635: 	for _, filter := range filters {
636: 		switch filter.FilterType {
637: 		case "name":
638: 			if !labRuntimeNameMatches(container.Names, filter.Match) {
639: 				return false
640: 			}
641: 		case "id":
642: 			if container.ID != filter.Match && !strings.HasPrefix(container.ID, filter.Match) {
643: 				return false
644: 			}
645: 		case "label":
646: 			if !labRuntimeLabelMatches(container.Labels, filter) {
647: 				return false
648: 			}
649: 		}
650: 	}
651: 
652: 	return true
653: }
654: 
655: func labRuntimeNameMatches(names []string, match string) bool {
656: 	for _, name := range names {
657: 		if name == match || strings.Contains(name, match) {
658: 			return true
659: 		}
660: 	}
661: 
662: 	return false
663: }
664: 
665: func labRuntimeLabelMatches(labels map[string]string, filter *clabtypes.GenericFilter) bool {
666: 	value, ok := labels[filter.Field]
667: 
668: 	switch filter.Operator {
669: 	case "exists":
670: 		return ok
671: 	case "!=":
672: 		return !ok || value != filter.Match
673: 	default:
674: 		return ok && value == filter.Match
675: 	}
676: }

678: func (c *CLab) copyLabRuntimeSavedFiles(
679: 	result *clablabruntime.SaveResult,
680: 	dstRoot string,
681: ) error {
682: 	for _, file := range result.Files {
683: 		if file.NodeName == "" || file.Name == "" {
684: 			continue
685: 		}
686: 
687: 		relPath, ok := cleanLabRuntimeSavedPath(file.Name)
688: 		if !ok {
689: 			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to copy unsafe saved config path %q", file.Name)
690: 		}
691: 
692: 		nodeDstDir := filepath.Join(dstRoot, file.NodeName)
693: 		dstPath := filepath.Join(nodeDstDir, relPath)
694: 		if err := os.MkdirAll(
695: 			filepath.Dir(dstPath),
696: 			clabconstants.PermissionsDirDefault,
697: 		); err != nil {
698: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create save dst directory %q: %w",
699: 				filepath.Dir(dstPath), err)
700: 		}
701: 
702: 		if file.LinkTarget != "" {
703: 			linkTarget, ok := cleanLabRuntimeSavedLinkTarget(file.LinkTarget)
704: 			if !ok {
705: 				return fmt.Errorf("refusing to create unsafe saved config symlink %q -> %q",
706: 					file.Name, file.LinkTarget)
707: 			}
708: 
709: 			_ = os.Remove(dstPath)
710: 			if err := os.Symlink(linkTarget, dstPath); err != nil {
711: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to create symlink %q -> %q: %w",
712: 					dstPath, linkTarget, err)
713: 			}
714: 
715: 			continue
716: 		}
717: 
718: 		mode := os.FileMode(file.Mode)
719: 		if mode == 0 {
720: 			mode = clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault
721: 		}
722: 
723: 		if err := os.WriteFile(dstPath, file.Data, mode); err != nil {
724: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write saved config %q: %w", dstPath, err)
725: 		}
726: 
727: 		log.Info(
728: 			"copied saved config",
729: 			"node", file.NodeName,
730: 			"dst", dstPath,
731: 		)
732: 	}
733: 
734: 	return nil
735: }
736: 
737: func cleanLabRuntimeSavedPath(name string) (string, bool) {
738: 	cleaned := filepath.Clean(name)
739: 	if cleaned == "." || filepath.IsAbs(cleaned) ||
740: 		strings.HasPrefix(cleaned, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) ||
741: 		cleaned == ".." {
742: 		return "", false
743: 	}
744: 
745: 	return cleaned, true
746: }
747: 
748: func cleanLabRuntimeSavedLinkTarget(target string) (string, bool) {
749: 	cleaned := filepath.Clean(target)
750: 	if filepath.IsAbs(cleaned) ||
751: 		strings.HasPrefix(cleaned, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) ||
752: 		cleaned == ".." {
753: 		return "", false
754: 	}
755: 
756: 	return cleaned, true
757: }

577: +package core
578: +
579: +import (

588: +	clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"
589: +	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
590: +)
591: +
592: +// The helpers in this file give library users per-node access to the lab selected by the CLab
593: +// (its topology file or WithTopologyName). Node names are accepted as the topology file spells
594: +// them or as a lab runtime sanitized them. Lab runtime calls act as the identity set with
595: +// WithLabRuntimeIdentity.
596: +
597: +// LocateLabRuntimeNodes reports the workload (namespace, pod, primary device container, Node
598: +// UID, exposed ports) of the given nodes, or of every node of the lab when none are given.
599: +func (c *CLab) LocateLabRuntimeNodes(
600: +	ctx context.Context,
601: +	nodeNames ...string,
602: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
603: +	locator, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLocator](c, "locating nodes")
604: +	if err != nil {
605: +		return nil, err
606: +	}
607: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
608: +		return nil, err
609: +	}
610: +
611: +	return locator.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
612: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
613: +		Nodes:    nodeNames,
614: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
615: +	})
616: +}
617: +
618: +// AttachLabRuntimeNode runs an interactive command in a node's device container (or in
619: +// req.Container) with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing. The lab name and identity
620: +// default to the CLab's. A command exiting nonzero returns a *labruntime.CommandExitError.
621: +func (c *CLab) AttachLabRuntimeNode(
622: +	ctx context.Context,
623: +	req clablabruntime.AttachRequest,
624: +	streams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,
625: +) error {
626: +	attacher, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeAttacher](c, "attaching to nodes")
627: +	if err != nil {
628: +		return err
629: +	}
630: +
631: +	if req.Name == "" {
632: +		if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
633: +			return err
634: +		}
635: +		req.Name = c.Config.Name
636: +	}
637: +	if req.Identity.IsZero() {
638: +		req.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity
639: +	}
640: +
641: +	return attacher.Attach(ctx, req, streams)
642: +}
643: +
644: +// DialLabRuntimeNodePort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node (SSH, web UIs) through the
645: +// lab runtime, such as a Kubernetes port-forward.
646: +func (c *CLab) DialLabRuntimeNodePort(
647: +	ctx context.Context,
648: +	nodeName string,
649: +	port int,
650: +) (net.Conn, error) {
651: +	forwarder, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodePortForwarder](
652: +		c, "port-forwarding to nodes")
653: +	if err != nil {
654: +		return nil, err
655: +	}
656: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
657: +		return nil, err
658: +	}
659: +
660: +	return forwarder.DialPort(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
661: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
662: +		Nodes:    []string{nodeName},
663: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
664: +	}, port)
665: +}
666: +
667: +// SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats reports the CPU and memory usage of the lab's running nodes. It
668: +// returns an error wrapping labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable when the cluster serves no resource
669: +// metrics.
670: +func (c *CLab) SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats(ctx context.Context) ([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, error) {
671: +	sampler, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeStatsSampler](
672: +		c, "sampling node stats")
673: +	if err != nil {
674: +		return nil, err
675: +	}
676: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
677: +		return nil, err
678: +	}
679: +
680: +	return sampler.SampleStats(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
681: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
682: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
683: +	})
684: +}
685: +
686: +// NodeLogOptions selects the node log NodeLogs writes.
687: +type NodeLogOptions struct {
688: +	// NodeName is the node whose log is written.
689: +	NodeName string
690: +	// Container overrides a lab runtime node's primary device container. Local runtimes do
691: +	// not support it.
692: +	Container string
693: +	// Tail limits the output to the last lines of the log; nil writes the whole log.
694: +	Tail *int64
695: +	// Follow keeps writing new log lines until the context ends.
696: +	Follow bool
697: +	// Timestamps prefixes every line with its timestamp.
698: +	Timestamps bool
699: +}
700: +
701: +// NodeLogs writes the log of a lab node with every runtime: the container log with Docker and
702: +// Podman, the device container log with a lab runtime. Lab runtimes write one combined stream to
703: +// stdout.
704: +func (c *CLab) NodeLogs(
705: +	ctx context.Context,
706: +	opts NodeLogOptions,
707: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
708: +) error {
709: +	if opts.NodeName == "" {
710: +		return fmt.Errorf("node name is required")
711: +	}
712: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
713: +		return err
714: +	}
715: +
716: +	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
717: +		streamer, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLogStreamer](
718: +			c, "streaming node logs")
719: +		if err != nil {
720: +			return err
721: +		}
722: +
723: +		return streamer.StreamLogs(ctx, clablabruntime.LogRequest{
724: +			Name:       c.Config.Name,
725: +			NodeName:   opts.NodeName,
726: +			Container:  opts.Container,
727: +			Tail:       opts.Tail,
728: +			Follow:     opts.Follow,
729: +			Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
730: +			Identity:   c.labRuntimeIdentity,
731: +		}, stdout)
732: +	}
733: +
734: +	if opts.Container != "" {
735: +		return fmt.Errorf("selecting a container is only supported with lab runtimes")
736: +	}
737: +
738: +	runtime, containerName, err := c.nodeContainer(ctx, opts.NodeName)
739: +	if err != nil {
740: +		return err
741: +	}
742: +
743: +	writer, ok := runtime.(clabruntime.ContainerLogWriter)
744: +	if !ok {
745: +		return fmt.Errorf("container runtime %q does not support node logs", runtime.GetName())
746: +	}
747: +
748: +	return writer.WriteContainerLogs(ctx, containerName, clabruntime.ContainerLogOptions{
749: +		Tail:       opts.Tail,
750: +		Follow:     opts.Follow,
751: +		Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
752: +	}, stdout, stderr)
753: +}

      "preview": "+      # kind does not serve on its own. kind kubelets use self-signed serving\n+      # certificates, hence --kubelet-insecure-tls.\n+      - name: Install metrics-server\n+        run: |\n+          kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server/releases/download/v0.9.0/components.yaml\n+          kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment metrics-server --type=json \\\n+            -p '[{\"op\":\"add\",\"path\":\"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/-\",\"value\":\"--kubelet-insecure-tls\"}]'\n+          kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/metrics-server --timeout=180s\n+          kubectl wait --for=condition=Available apiservice/v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io --timeout=180s\n+\n       - name: Install Clabernetes\n         run: |\n+          # create the mounted directories as the runner user, otherwise docker\n+          # creates them (and ~/.cache, which holds the Go build cache) as root\n+          mkdir -p \"${HOME}/.kube\" \"${HOME}/.helm\" \"${HOME}/.config/helm\" \"${HOME}/.cache/helm\"\n           docker run --network host --rm \\\n             -v \"${HOME}/.kube:/root/.kube\" \\\n             -v \"${HOME}/.helm:/root/.helm\" \\\n             -v \"${HOME}/.config/helm:/root/.config/helm\" \\\n             -v \"${HOME}/.cache/helm:/root/.cache/helm\" \\",

Lab runtime calls act as the identity set with\n+// WithLabRuntimeIdentity.\n+\n+// LocateLabRuntimeNodes reports the workload (namespace, pod, primary device container, Node\n+// UID, exposed ports) of the given nodes, or of every node of the lab when none are given.\n+func (c *CLab) LocateLabRuntimeNodes(\n+\tctx context.Context,\n+\tnodeNames ...string,\n+) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {\n+\tlocator, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLocator](c, \"locating nodes\")\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn nil, err\n+\t}\n+\tif err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {\n+\t\treturn nil, err\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn locator.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{\n+\t\tName:     c.Config.Name,\n+\t\tNodes:    nodeNames,\n+\t\tIdentity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,\n+\t})\n+}\n+\n+// AttachLabRuntimeNode runs an interactive command in a node's device container (or in\n+// req.Container) with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing. The lab name and identity\n+// default to the CLab's. A command exiting nonzero returns a *labruntime.CommandExitError.\n+func (c *CLab) AttachLabRuntimeNode(\n+\tctx context.Context,\n+\treq clablabruntime.AttachRequest,\n+\tstreams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,\n+) error {\n+\tattacher, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeAttacher](c, \"attaching to nodes\")\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\n+\tif req.Name == \"\" {\n+\t\tif err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {\n+\t\t\treturn err\n+\t\t}\n+\t\treq.Name = c.Config.Name\n+\t}\n+\tif req.Identity.IsZero() {\n+\t\treq.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn attacher.Attach(ctx, req, streams)\n+}\n+\n+// DialLabRuntimeNodePort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node (SSH, web UIs) through the\n+// lab runtime, such as a Kubernetes port-forward.\n+func (c *CLab) DialLabRuntimeNodePort(\n+\tctx context.Context,\n+\tnodeName string,\n+\tport int,\n+) (net.Conn, error) {\n+\tforwarder, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodePortForwarder](\n+\t\tc, \"port-forwarding to nodes\")\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn nil, err\n+\t}\n+\tif err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {\n+\t\treturn nil, err\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn forwarder.DialPort(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{\n+\t\tName:     c.Config.Name,\n+\t\tNodes:    []string{nodeName},\n+\t\tIdentity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,\n+\t}, port)\n+}\n+\n+// SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats reports the CPU and memory usage of the lab's running nodes. Local runtimes do\n+\t// not support it.\n+\tContainer string\n+\t// Tail limits the output to the last lines of the log; nil writes the whole log.\n+\tTail *int64\n+\t// Follow keeps writing new log lines until the context ends.\n+\tFollow bool\n+\t// Timestamps prefixes every line with its timestamp.\n+\tTimestamps bool\n+}\n+\n+// NodeLogs writes the log of a lab node with every runtime: the container log with Docker and\n+// Podman, the device container log with a lab runtime. Lab runtimes write one combined stream to\n+// stdout.\n+func (c *CLab) NodeLogs(\n+\tctx context.Context,\n+\topts NodeLogOptions,\n+\tstdout, stderr io.Writer,\n+) error {\n+\tif opts.NodeName == \"\" {\n+\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"node name is required\")\n+\t}\n+\tif err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\n+\tif c.LabRuntime != nil {\n+\t\tstreamer, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLogStreamer](\n+\t\t\tc, \"streaming node logs\")\n+\t\tif err != nil {\n+\t\t\treturn err\n+\t\t}\n+\n+\t\treturn streamer.StreamLogs(ctx, clablabruntime.LogRequest{\n+\t\t\tName:       c.Config.Name,\n+\t\t\tNodeName:   opts.NodeName,\n+\t\t\tContainer:  opts.Container,\n+\t\t\tTail:       opts.Tail,\n+\t\t\tFollow:     opts.Follow,\n+\t\t\tTimestamps: opts.Timestamps,\n+\t\t\tIdentity:   c.labRuntimeIdentity,\n+\t\t}, stdout)\n+\t}\n+\n+\tif opts.Container != \"\" {\n+\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"selecting a container is only supported with lab runtimes\")\n+\t}\n+\n+\truntime, containerName, err := c.nodeContainer(ctx, opts.NodeName)\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\n+\twriter, ok := runtime.(clabruntime.ContainerLogWriter)\n+\tif !ok {\n+\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"container runtime %q does not support node logs\", runtime.GetName())\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn writer.WriteContainerLogs(ctx, containerName, clabruntime.ContainerLogOptions{\n+\t\tTail:       opts.Tail,\n+\t\tFollow:     opts.Follow,\n+\t\tTimestamps: opts.Timestamps,\n+\t}, stdout, stderr)\n+}\n+\n+// nodeContainer finds the container of a lab node in the local container runtimes by the lab\n+// and node name labels.\n+func (c *CLab) nodeContainer(\n+\tctx context.Context,",

1351: @@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
1352: +# logs command
1353: +
1354: +### Description
1355: +
1356: +The `logs` command shows the log of a lab node. With Docker and Podman it is the node container's log, with the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#logs) the log of the node's primary device container in its pod.
1357: +
1358: +--8<-- "docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags"
1359: +
1360: +### Usage
1361: +
1362: +`containerlab [global-flags] logs [local-flags]`
1363: +
1364: +### Flags
1365: +
1366: +#### topology | name
1367: +
1368: +Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.
1369: +
1370: +#### node
1371: +
1372: +Use the local `--node | -n` flag to select the node. The flag is required. With the c9s runtime the node name is accepted as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`).
1373: +
1374: +#### tail
1375: +
1376: +The local `--tail` flag limits the output to the last N lines of the log. The default `-1` shows the whole log; `--tail 0` shows no previous lines, which is useful with `--follow`.
1377: +
1378: +#### follow
1379: +
1380: +The local `--follow | -f` flag keeps streaming new log lines until the command is interrupted.
1381: +
1382: +#### timestamps
1383: +
1384: +The local `--timestamps` flag prefixes every line with its timestamp in RFC 3339 format.
1385: +
1386: +### Output
1387: +
1388: +The log goes to stdout. With Docker and Podman, the container's stderr goes to stderr, unless the container has a TTY; Kubernetes returns one combined stream, written to stdout.
1389: +
1390: +### Examples
1391: +
1392: +#### Show the whole log of a node
1393: +
1394: +```bash
1395: +containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1
1396: +```
1397: +
1398: +#### Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps
1399: +
1400: +```bash
1401: +containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps
1402: +```
1403: +
1404: +#### Show the device log of a node in a c9s lab
1405: +
1406: +```bash
1407: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 50
1408: +```
1409: diff --git a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
1410: index 88e63a4..18dc015 100644
1411: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
1412: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
1413: @@ -528,10 +528,24 @@ needs to reach the cluster.
1414:  If any selected command returns nonzero, or pod exec itself fails, the outer
1415:  `containerlab exec` also returns nonzero. Successful and failed results that
1416:  were received are still printed, so automation can use both the output and the
1417:  process exit status.
1418:  
1419: +## Logs
1420: +
1421: +`logs` shows the log of a node's primary device container, the same container
1422: +`exec` uses:
1423: +
1424: +```bash
1425: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs -t topo.clab.yml -n srl1
1426: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps
1427: +```
1428: +
1429: +It reads the `pods/log` subresource of the node's pod, so RBAC must allow
1430: +`get` on `pods/log`. Kubernetes returns stdout and stderr as one stream. See
1431: +the [`logs` command](../../cmd/logs.md) for the flags.
1432: +
1433:  ## Start, stop, and restart
1434:  
1435:  Node lifecycle commands operate on the kubernetes Deployments created by
1436:  Clabernetes.
1437:  
1438: @@ -782,10 +796,66 @@ token:
1439:  ```bash
1440:  kubectl -n <namespace> annotate node.c9s.run <node> \
1441:    c9s.run/device-state-reset=$(date +%s) --overwrite
1442:  ```
1443:  
1444: +## Node access from Go
1445: +
1446: +Programs that use containerlab as a Go library, such as clab-api-server, open
1447: +terminals, follow logs, reach node ports and read resource usage through
1448: +optional lab runtime interfaces in `github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime`,
1449: +implemented by the c9s runtime:
1450: +
1451: +| Interface | Method | What it does |
1452: +|---|---|---|
1453: +| `NodeLocator` | `LocateNode(ctx, NodeRequest) ([]NodeLocation, error)` | the namespace, pod, primary device container, Node UID, exposed ports and LoadBalancer address of nodes |
1454: +| `NodeAttacher` | `Attach(ctx, AttachRequest, AttachStreams) error` | an interactive exec with stdin, an optional TTY and a resize channel, in the device container or a chosen container |
1455: +| `NodeLogStreamer` | `StreamLogs(ctx, LogRequest, io.Writer) error` | the device container log, with tail, follow and timestamps |
1456: +| `NodePortForwarder` | `DialPort(ctx, NodeRequest, port) (net.Conn, error)` | a connection to a TCP port of the node's pod through `pods/portforward` (SSH, web UIs) |
1457: +| `NodeStatsSampler` | `SampleStats(ctx, InspectRequest) ([]NodeStats, error)` | CPU and memory per node from `metrics.k8s.io` PodMetrics, summing the node's device containers; without the metrics API the error wraps `labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable` |
1458: +
1459: +The `core` package wraps them per lab and node name, accepting the node name
1460: +as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized:
1461: +`CLab.LocateLabRuntimeNodes`, `CLab.AttachLabRuntimeNode`,
1462: +`CLab.DialLabRuntimeNodePort`, `CLab.SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats` and
1463: +`CLab.NodeLogs`, which also serves Docker and Podman.
1464: +
1465: +```go
1466: +c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(
1467: +	clabcore.WithRuntime("c9s", nil),
1468: +	clabcore.WithTopologyName("clos"),
1469: +	clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity(clablabruntime.Identity{
1470: +		User:   "clab:alice",
1471: +		Groups: []string{"clab:users"},
1472: +	}),
1473: +)
1474: +if err != nil {
1475: +	return err
1476: +}
1477: +
1478: +conn, err := c.DialLabRuntimeNodePort(ctx, "srl1", 22)
1479: +```
1480: +
1481: +### Acting as a user
1482: +
1483: +A server that runs labs for many users acts as each user, so the cluster's RBAC
1484: +decides what a user may do and its audit log names the user:
1485: +
1486: +- `labruntime.Identity{User, Groups}` is Kubernetes user impersonation.
1487: +  `labruntime.Config.Identity` sets it for a runtime, every request type has an
1488: +  `Identity` field that overrides it per call, and
1489: +  `clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity` sets it for every call of a `CLab`.
1490: +- The c9s runtime builds one set of Kubernetes clients per identity from the
1491: +  kubeconfig and caches them. The impersonation applies to every transport:
1492: +  REST calls, watches, log streams, and the websocket and SPDY connections of
1493: +  exec, attach and port-forward.
1494: +- Without an identity, the kubeconfig is used as it is. The CLI has no
1495: +  impersonation flags: a CLI user acts with their own kubeconfig rights.
1496: +
1497: +The kubeconfig identity then needs the `impersonate` verb on the users and
1498: +groups it acts as.
1499: +
1500:  ## RBAC requirements
1501:  
1502:  The kube identity used by the outer containerlab process must be able to:
1503:  
1504:  - get, create, and delete namespaces when using automatic per-lab namespaces
1505: @@ -796,10 +866,13 @@ The kube identity used by the outer containerlab process must be able to:
1506:  - list and watch Pods
1507:  - list, get, and update Deployments
1508:  - create, get, list, update, and delete ConfigMaps used for local files
1509:  - exec into device Pods with `pods/exec`
1510:  - list and delete PersistentVolumeClaims for `destroy --cleanup`
1511: +- read container logs with `pods/log` for `logs`
1512: +- port-forward with `pods/portforward` for `NodePortForwarder`
1513: +- list `pods.metrics.k8s.io` for `NodeStatsSampler`
1514:  
1515:  Useful checks:
1516:  
1517:  ```bash
1518:  kubectl auth can-i get namespaces

1621: +	}
1622: +
1623: +	if len(req.Nodes) == 0 {
1624: +		locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(state.Nodes))
1625: +		for _, node := range state.Nodes {

1627: +		}
1628: +
1629: +		return locations, nil
1630: +	}
1631: +
1632: +	locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(req.Nodes))
1633: +	for _, nodeName := range req.Nodes {
1634: +		resolved, ok := resolveKnownNodeName(nodes, nodeName)
1635: +		if !ok {

1637: +				nodeName, state.Namespace, state.Name)

1768: +// newExecutor streams a pod exec over websockets, falling back to SPDY when the API server
1769: +// does not upgrade the websocket, like kubectl. The websocket executor reports upgrade
1770: +// failures with the k8s.io/streaming error types. Both transports are built from the runtime's
1771: +// rest config, so they carry its impersonation headers.
1772: +func (r *Runtime) newExecutor(execURL *url.URL) (remotecommand.Executor, error) {
1773: +	websocketExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewWebSocketExecutor(
1774: +		r.restConfig, http.MethodGet, execURL.String())
1775: +	if err != nil {
1776: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes websocket exec executor: %w", err)
1777: +	}
1778: +
1779: +	spdyExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewSPDYExecutor(r.restConfig, http.MethodPost, execURL)
1780: +	if err != nil {
1781: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes exec executor: %w", err)
1782: +	}
1783: +
1784: +	return remotecommand.NewFallbackExecutor(websocketExecutor, spdyExecutor,
1785: +		func(err error) bool {
1786: +			return streamhttp.IsUpgradeFailure(err) || streamhttp.IsHTTPSProxyError(err)
1787: +		})
1788: +}

1790: +// terminalSizeQueue adapts a resize channel to the remotecommand size queue.

1793: +	resize <-chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize

1795: +
1796: +func newTerminalSizeQueue(
1797: +	ctx context.Context,
1798: +	resize <-chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize,

1800: +	return &terminalSizeQueue{ctx: ctx, resize: resize}

1803: +// Next blocks until the next size change; nil ends resizing.

1805: +	select {

1807: +		return nil
1808: +	case size, ok := <-q.resize:

1810: +			return nil
1811: +		}
1812: +
1813: +		return &remotecommand.TerminalSize{Width: size.Width, Height: size.Height}
1814: +	}
1815: +}

1893: +// dialPodPort opens a forwarded connection to a pod port over SPDY. The transport is built
1894: +// from the runtime's rest config, so it carries its impersonation headers.
1895: +func (r *Runtime) dialPodPort(namespace, pod string, port int) (net.Conn, error) {
1896: +	forwardURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
1897: +		Resource("pods").
1898: +		Name(pod).
1899: +		Namespace(namespace).
1900: +		SubResource("portforward").URL()
1901: +
1902: +	transport, upgrader, err := spdy.RoundTripperFor(r.restConfig)
1903: +	if err != nil {
1904: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes port-forward transport: %w", err)
1905: +	}
1906: +
1907: +	dialer := spdy.NewDialer(upgrader, &http.Client{Transport: transport}, http.MethodPost,
1908: +		forwardURL)
1909: +
1910: +	streamConn, _, err := dialer.Dial(portforward.PortForwardProtocolV1Name)
1911: +	if err != nil {
1912: +		return nil, err
1913: +	}
1914: +
1915: +	conn, err := newPortForwardConn(streamConn, port)
1916: +	if err != nil {
1917: +		_ = streamConn.Close()
1918: +
1919: +		return nil, err
1920: +	}
1921: +
1922: +	return conn, nil
1923: +}
1924: +
1925: +// newPortForwardConn opens the error and data streams of one forwarded connection and returns
1926: +// one end of an in-memory pipe whose other end is copied to and from the data stream. The pipe
1927: +// gives the caller a complete net.Conn, deadlines included.
1928: +func newPortForwardConn(streamConn httpstream.Connection, port int) (net.Conn, error) {
1929: +	requestID := strconv.FormatInt(portForwardRequestID.Add(1), 10)
1930: +
1931: +	headers := http.Header{}
1932: +	headers.Set(corev1.StreamType, corev1.StreamTypeError)
1933: +	headers.Set(corev1.PortHeader, strconv.Itoa(port))
1934: +	headers.Set(corev1.PortForwardRequestIDHeader, requestID)
1935: +
1936: +	errorStream, err := streamConn.CreateStream(headers)
1937: +	if err != nil {
1938: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create the error stream: %w", err)
1939: +	}
1940: +	// the client sends nothing on the error stream; Close only half-closes it, so the API
1941: +	// server can still report failures on it
1942: +	_ = errorStream.Close()
1943: +
1944: +	headers.Set(corev1.StreamType, corev1.StreamTypeData)
1945: +	dataStream, err := streamConn.CreateStream(headers)
1946: +	if err != nil {
1947: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create the data stream: %w", err)
1948: +	}
1949: +
1950: +	local, remote := net.Pipe()
1951: +
1952: +	var closeOnce sync.Once
1953: +	closeAll := func() {
1954: +		closeOnce.Do(func() {
1955: +			_ = remote.Close()
1956: +			_ = dataStream.Reset()
1957: +			_ = streamConn.Close()
1958: +		})
1959: +	}
1960: +
1961: +	go func() {
1962: +		// the API server reports a failure to reach the port on the error stream
1963: +		message, _ := io.ReadAll(errorStream)
1964: +		if len(message) != 0 {
1965: +			log.Warn("Port forward failed", "port", port, "error", string(message))
1966: +			_ = remote.Close()
1967: +		}
1968: +	}()
1969: +
1970: +	go func() {
1971: +		defer closeAll()
1972: +		_, _ = io.Copy(remote, dataStream)
1973: +	}()
1974: +
1975: +	go func() {
1976: +		defer closeAll()
1977: +		_, _ = io.Copy(dataStream, remote)
1978: +	}()
1979: +
1980: +	go func() {
1981: +		<-streamConn.CloseChan()
1982: +		closeAll()
1983: +	}()
1984: +
1985: +	return local, nil
1986: +}

With Docker and Podman it is the node container's log, with the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#logs) the log of the node's primary device container in its pod.\n1357: +\n1358: +--8<-- \"docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags\"\n1359: +\n1360: +### Usage\n1361: +\n1362: +`containerlab [global-flags] logs [local-flags]`\n1363: +\n1364: +### Flags\n1365: +\n1366: +#### topology | name\n1367: +\n1368: +Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. With the c9s runtime the node name is accepted as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`).\n1373: +\n1374: +#### tail\n1375: +\n1376: +The local `--tail` flag limits the output to the last N lines of the log. The default `-1` shows the whole log; `--tail 0` shows no previous lines, which is useful with `--follow`.\n1377: +\n1378: +#### follow\n1379: +\n1380: +The local `--follow | -f` flag keeps streaming new log lines until the command is interrupted.\n1381: +\n1382: +#### timestamps\n1383: +\n1384: +The local `--timestamps` flag prefixes every line with its timestamp in RFC 3339 format.\n1385: +\n1386: +### Output\n1387: +\n1388: +The log goes to stdout. With Docker and Podman, the container's stderr goes to stderr, unless the container has a TTY; Kubernetes returns one combined stream, written to stdout.\n1389: +\n1390: +### Examples\n1391: +\n1392: +#### Show the whole log of a node\n1393: +\n1394: +```bash\n1395: +containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1\n1396: +```\n1397: +\n1398: +#### Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps\n1399: +\n1400: +```bash\n1401: +containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps\n1402: +```\n1403: +\n1404: +#### Show the device log of a node in a c9s lab\n1405: +\n1406: +```bash\n1407: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 50\n1408: +```\n1409: diff --git a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n1410: index 88e63a4..18dc015 100644\n1411: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n1412: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n1413: @@ -528,10 +528,24 @@ needs to reach the cluster.\n1414:  If any selected command returns nonzero, or pod exec itself fails, the outer\n1415:  `containerlab exec` also returns nonzero. With Docker and Podman it is the node container's log, with the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#logs) the log of the node's primary device container in its pod.\n+\n+--8<-- \"docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags\"\n+\n+### Usage\n+\n+`containerlab [global-flags] logs [local-flags]`\n+\n+### Flags\n+\n+#### topology | name\n+\n+Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.\n+\n+#### node\n+\n+Use the local `--node | -n` flag to select the node. The flag is required. With the c9s runtime the node name is accepted as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`).\n+\n+#### tail\n+\n+The local `--tail` flag limits the output to the last N lines of the log. The default `-1` shows the whole log; `--tail 0` shows no previous lines, which is useful with `--follow`.\n+\n+#### follow\n+\n+The local `--follow | -f` flag keeps streaming new log lines until the command is interrupted.\n+\n+#### timestamps\n+\n+The local `--timestamps` flag prefixes every line with its timestamp in RFC 3339 format.\n+\n+### Output\n+\n+The log goes to stdout. With Docker and Podman, the container's stderr goes to stderr, unless the container has a TTY; Kubernetes returns one combined stream, written to stdout.\n+\n+### Examples\n+\n+#### Show the whole log of a node\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1\n+```\n+\n+#### Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps\n+```\n+\n+#### Show the device log of a node in a c9s lab\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 50\n+```\ndiff --git a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\nindex 88e63a4..18dc015 100644\n--- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n+++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n@@ -528,10 +528,24 @@ needs to reach the cluster.\n If any selected command returns nonzero, or pod exec itself fails, the outer\n `containerlab exec` also returns nonzero. 2216: +func TestLocateNode(t *testing.T) {
2217: +	t.Parallel()
2218: +
2219: +	r := accessTestRuntime(t)
2220: +
2221: +	all, err := r.LocateNode(context.Background(), clablabruntime.NodeRequest{Name: "lab1"})
2222: +	if err != nil {
2223: +		t.Fatal(err)
2224: +	}
2225: +	if len(all) != 1 {
2226: +		t.Fatalf("locations = %+v, want r1", all)
2227: +	}
2228: +
2229: +	// the topology spells the node "R1"; Kubernetes carries it as "r1"
2230: +	named, err := r.LocateNode(context.Background(), clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
2231: +		Name:  "lab1",
2232: +		Nodes: []string{"R1"},
2233: +	})
2234: +	if err != nil {
2235: +		t.Fatal(err)
2236: +	}
2237: +	got := named[0]
2238: +	if got.NodeName != "r1" || got.Namespace != "lab-ns" || got.Pod != "lab1-r1-abc" ||
2239: +		got.Container != "node-r1-x" || got.NodeUID != "uid-r1" ||
2240: +		len(got.ExposedPorts) != 1 || got.ExposedPorts[0].Port != 22 {
2241: +		t.Fatalf("location = %+v", got)
2242: +	}
2243: +
2244: +	if _, err := r.LocateNode(context.Background(), clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
2245: +		Name:  "lab1",
2246: +		Nodes: []string{"missing"},
2247: +	}); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "missing") {
2248: +		t.Fatalf("unknown node error = %v", err)
2249: +	}
2250: +}

2252: +func TestStreamLogsTargetsTheDeviceContainer(t *testing.T) {
2253: +	t.Parallel()
2254: +
2255: +	r := accessTestRuntime(t)
2256: +	tail := int64(25)
2257: +
2258: +	var out strings.Builder
2259: +	if err := r.StreamLogs(context.Background(), clablabruntime.LogRequest{
2260: +		Name:       "lab1",
2261: +		NodeName:   "R1",
2262: +		Tail:       &tail,
2263: +		Follow:     true,
2264: +		Timestamps: true,
2265: +	}, &out); err != nil {
2266: +		t.Fatal(err)
2267: +	}
2268: +	if out.String() != "fake logs" {
2269: +		t.Fatalf("log output = %q", out.String())
2270: +	}
2271: +
2272: +	var opts *corev1.PodLogOptions
2273: +	for _, action := range r.kubeClient.(*kubefake.Clientset).Actions() {
2274: +		if action.GetSubresource() != "log" {
2275: +			continue
2276: +		}
2277: +		generic, ok := action.(k8stesting.GenericActionImpl)
2278: +		if !ok {
2279: +			continue
2280: +		}
2281: +		opts, _ = generic.Value.(*corev1.PodLogOptions)
2282: +	}
2283: +	if opts == nil || opts.Container != "node-r1-x" || !opts.Follow || !opts.Timestamps ||
2284: +		opts.TailLines == nil || *opts.TailLines != 25 {
2285: +		t.Fatalf("pod log options = %+v", opts)
2286: +	}
2287: +
2288: +	if err := r.StreamLogs(context.Background(), clablabruntime.LogRequest{
2289: +		Name:      "lab1",
2290: +		NodeName:  "r1",
2291: +		Container: "clabwire",
2292: +	}, io.Discard); err != nil {
2293: +		t.Fatal(err)
2294: +	}
2295: +}

2327: +	return &unstructured.Unstructured{Object: map[string]any{
2328: +		"apiVersion": "metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1",
2329: +		"kind":       "PodMetrics",
2330: +		"metadata":   map[string]any{"name": name, "namespace": "lab-ns"},
2331: +		"timestamp":  "2026-10-27T10:00:00Z",
2332: +		"window":     "15s",
2333: +		"containers": entries,
2334: +	}}
2335: +}

2390: +func TestTerminalSizeQueue(t *testing.T) {
2391: +	t.Parallel()
2392: +
2393: +	resize := make(chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize, 1)
2394: +	queue := newTerminalSizeQueue(context.Background(), resize)
2395: +
2396: +	resize <- clablabruntime.TerminalSize{Width: 120, Height: 40}
2397: +	if size := queue.Next(); size == nil || size.Width != 120 || size.Height != 40 {
2398: +		t.Fatalf("Next() = %+v", size)

2400: +
2401: +	close(resize)
2402: +	if size := queue.Next(); size != nil {

2405: +

2407: +	cancel()
2408: +	if size := newTerminalSizeQueue(
2409: +		ctx,
2410: +		make(chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize),
2411: +	).Next(); size != nil {
2412: +		t.Fatalf("Next() after cancel = %+v, want nil", size)
2413: +	}
2414: +}

2416: +// impersonationRecorder is an API server stub that records the impersonation headers of every
2417: +// request and answers with a Status error.
2418: +type impersonationRecorder struct {
2419: +	mu       sync.Mutex
2420: +	requests []recordedRequest
2421: +}
2422: +
2423: +type recordedRequest struct {
2424: +	method string
2425: +	path   string
2426: +	user   string
2427: +	groups []string
2428: +}
2429: +
2430: +func (rec *impersonationRecorder) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
2431: +	rec.mu.Lock()
2432: +	rec.requests = append(rec.requests, recordedRequest{
2433: +		method: req.Method,
2434: +		path:   req.URL.Path,
2435: +		user:   req.Header.Get("Impersonate-User"),
2436: +		groups: req.Header.Values("Impersonate-Group"),
2437: +	})
2438: +	rec.mu.Unlock()
2439: +
2440: +	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
2441: +	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusForbidden)
2442: +	_, _ = io.WriteString(w,
2443: +		`{"kind":"Status","apiVersion":"v1","status":"Failure","reason":"Forbidden","code":403}`)
2444: +}
2445: +
2446: +func (rec *impersonationRecorder) take() []recordedRequest {
2447: +	rec.mu.Lock()
2448: +	defer rec.mu.Unlock()
2449: +
2450: +	requests := rec.requests
2451: +	rec.requests = nil
2452: +
2453: +	return requests
2454: +}

2456: +func TestIdentityImpersonatesOnEveryTransport(t *testing.T) {
2457: +	t.Parallel()
2458: +
2459: +	recorder := &impersonationRecorder{}
2460: +	server := httptest.NewServer(recorder)
2461: +	defer server.Close()
2462: +
2463: +	r := &Runtime{
2464: +		identity: clablabruntime.Identity{User: "clab:default"},
2465: +		clients: &clientLoader{
2466: +			loadConfig: func() (*rest.Config, string, error) {
2467: +				return &rest.Config{Host: server.URL}, "", nil
2468: +			},
2469: +			newClients: newKubeClients,
2470: +		},
2471: +	}
2472: +	alice := clablabruntime.Identity{
2473: +		User:   "clab:alice",
2474: +		Groups: []string{"clab:users", "clab:admins"},
2475: +	}
2476: +
2477: +	view, err := r.connect(alice)
2478: +	if err != nil {
2479: +		t.Fatal(err)
2480: +	}
2481: +	again, err := r.connect(alice)
2482: +	if err != nil || again.kubeClient != view.kubeClient {
2483: +		t.Fatal("clients of one identity were not cached")
2484: +	}
2485: +	defaultView, err := r.connect(clablabruntime.Identity{})
2486: +	if err != nil || defaultView.kubeClient == view.kubeClient {
2487: +		t.Fatal("the configured identity shares the clients of another identity")
2488: +	}
2489: +
2490: +	ctx := context.Background()
2491: +	pod := &corev1.Pod{ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Name: "lab1-r1-abc", Namespace: "lab-ns"}}
2492: +
2493: +	// REST
2494: +	_, _ = r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1", Identity: alice})
2495: +	// pod exec: websocket first, then SPDY
2496: +	_, _, _, _ = view.execInPod(ctx, pod, "node-r1-x", []string{"true"})
2497: +	// port-forward over SPDY
2498: +	if conn, err := view.dialPodPort("lab-ns", "lab1-r1-abc", 22); err == nil {
2499: +		_ = conn.Close()
2500: +	}
2501: +	// a call without identity uses the configured one
2502: +	_, _ = r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1"})
2503: +
2504: +	requests := recorder.take()
2505: +	seen := map[string]bool{}
2506: +	for _, req := range requests {
2507: +		switch {
2508: +		case strings.HasSuffix(req.path, "/exec"):
2509: +			seen["exec-"+req.method] = true
2510: +		case strings.HasSuffix(req.path, "/portforward"):
2511: +			seen["portforward"] = true
2512: +		default:
2513: +			seen["rest-"+req.user] = true
2514: +		}
2515: +
2516: +		if req.user == "clab:default" {
2517: +			if len(req.groups) != 0 {
2518: +				t.Fatalf("configured identity sent groups: %+v", req)
2519: +			}
2520: +			continue
2521: +		}
2522: +		if req.user != alice.User || strings.Join(req.groups, ",") != "clab:users,clab:admins" {
2523: +			t.Fatalf("request without alice's impersonation: %+v", req)
2524: +		}
2525: +	}
2526: +
2527: +	for _, want := range []string{
2528: +		"rest-clab:alice", "exec-GET", "exec-POST", "portforward", "rest-clab:default",
2529: +	} {
2530: +		if !seen[want] {
2531: +			t.Fatalf("no %s request recorded: %+v", want, requests)
2532: +		}
2533: +	}
2534: +}

3397: +// WriteContainerLogs writes a container's log through the Podman API.
3398: +func (r *PodmanRuntime) WriteContainerLogs(
3399: +	ctx context.Context,
3400: +	containerName string,
3401: +	opts runtime.ContainerLogOptions,
3402: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
3403: +) error {
3404: +	ctx, err := r.connect(ctx)
3405: +	if err != nil {
3406: +		return err
3407: +	}
3408: +
3409: +	stdoutCh := make(chan string)
3410: +	stderrCh := make(chan string)
3411: +	done := make(chan error, 1)
3412: +
3413: +	go func() {
3414: +		logOpts := new(containers.LogOptions).
3415: +			WithStdout(true).
3416: +			WithStderr(true).
3417: +			WithFollow(opts.Follow).
3418: +			WithTimestamps(opts.Timestamps).
3419: +			WithTail(runtime.LogTail(opts.Tail))
3420: +		done <- containers.Logs(ctx, containerName, logOpts, stdoutCh, stderrCh)
3421: +	}()
3422: +
3423: +	// the bindings send on the channels without watching the context; keep draining them
3424: +	// after an early return so the sender can finish
3425: +	drain := func() {
3426: +		go func() {
3427: +			for {
3428: +				select {
3429: +				case <-stdoutCh:
3430: +				case <-stderrCh:
3431: +				case <-done:
3432: +					return
3433: +				}
3434: +			}
3435: +		}()
3436: +	}
3437: +
3438: +	for {
3439: +		select {
3440: +		case line := <-stdoutCh:
3441: +			if _, err := io.WriteString(stdout, line); err != nil {
3442: +				drain()
3443: +				return err
3444: +			}
3445: +		case line := <-stderrCh:
3446: +			if _, err := io.WriteString(stderr, line); err != nil {
3447: +				drain()
3448: +				return err
3449: +			}
3450: +		case err := <-done:
3451: +			if err != nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
3452: +				return fmt.Errorf("failed to get container logs: %w", err)
3453: +			}
3454: +
3455: +			return nil
3456: +		}
3457: +	}
3458: +}

3490: +	Tail *int64
3491: +	// Follow keeps writing new log lines until the context ends.
3492: +	Follow bool

3494: +	Timestamps bool
3495: +}

3499: +	// WriteContainerLogs writes the container's stdout and stderr to the given writers. A
3500: +	// container with a TTY has one combined stream, written to stdout.
3501: +	WriteContainerLogs(
3502: +		ctx context.Context,

3513: +	}

On the normal `done` path, the binding call containers.Logs has returned, so no more sends occur after done is received — well, actually done is sent after containers.Logs returns, so once done is in the buffered channel (cap 1), the goroutine has finished sending on stdoutCh/stderrCh. 2416: +// impersonationRecorder is an API server stub that records the impersonation headers of every
2417: +// request and answers with a Status error.
2418: +type impersonationRecorder struct {
2419: +	mu       sync.Mutex
2420: +	requests []recordedRequest
2421: +}
2422: +
2423: +type recordedRequest struct {
2424: +	method string
2425: +	path   string
2426: +	user   string
2427: +	groups []string
2428: +}
2429: +
2430: +func (rec *impersonationRecorder) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
2431: +	rec.mu.Lock()
2432: +	rec.requests = append(rec.requests, recordedRequest{
2433: +		method: req.Method,
2434: +		path:   req.URL.Path,
2435: +		user:   req.Header.Get("Impersonate-User"),
2436: +		groups: req.Header.Values("Impersonate-Group"),
2437: +	})
2438: +	rec.mu.Unlock()
2439: +
2440: +	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
2441: +	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusForbidden)
2442: +	_, _ = io.WriteString(w,
2443: +		`{"kind":"Status","apiVersion":"v1","status":"Failure","reason":"Forbidden","code":403}`)
2444: +}
2445: +
2446: +func (rec *impersonationRecorder) take() []recordedRequest {
2447: +	rec.mu.Lock()
2448: +	defer rec.mu.Unlock()
2449: +
2450: +	requests := rec.requests
2451: +	rec.requests = nil
2452: +
2453: +	return requests
2454: +}

576: @@ -0,0 +1,246 @@
577: +package core
578: +
579: +import (
580: +	"context"
581: +	"fmt"
582: +	"io"
583: +	"net"
584: +	"sort"
585: +
586: +	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
587: +	clablabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime"
588: +	clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"
589: +	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
590: +)
591: +
592: +// The helpers in this file give library users per-node access to the lab selected by the CLab
593: +// (its topology file or WithTopologyName). Node names are accepted as the topology file spells
594: +// them or as a lab runtime sanitized them. Lab runtime calls act as the identity set with
595: +// WithLabRuntimeIdentity.
596: +
597: +// LocateLabRuntimeNodes reports the workload (namespace, pod, primary device container, Node
598: +// UID, exposed ports) of the given nodes, or of every node of the lab when none are given.
599: +func (c *CLab) LocateLabRuntimeNodes(
600: +	ctx context.Context,
601: +	nodeNames ...string,
602: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
603: +	locator, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLocator](c, "locating nodes")
604: +	if err != nil {
605: +		return nil, err
606: +	}
607: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
608: +		return nil, err
609: +	}
610: +
611: +	return locator.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
612: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
613: +		Nodes:    nodeNames,
614: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
615: +	})
616: +}
617: +
618: +// AttachLabRuntimeNode runs an interactive command in a node's device container (or in
619: +// req.Container) with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing. The lab name and identity
620: +// default to the CLab's. A command exiting nonzero returns a *labruntime.CommandExitError.
621: +func (c *CLab) AttachLabRuntimeNode(
622: +	ctx context.Context,
623: +	req clablabruntime.AttachRequest,
624: +	streams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,
625: +) error {
626: +	attacher, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeAttacher](c, "attaching to nodes")
627: +	if err != nil {
628: +		return err
629: +	}
630: +
631: +	if req.Name == "" {
632: +		if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
633: +			return err
634: +		}
635: +		req.Name = c.Config.Name
636: +	}
637: +	if req.Identity.IsZero() {
638: +		req.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity
639: +	}
640: +
641: +	return attacher.Attach(ctx, req, streams)
642: +}
643: +
644: +// DialLabRuntimeNodePort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node (SSH, web UIs) through the
645: +// lab runtime, such as a Kubernetes port-forward.
646: +func (c *CLab) DialLabRuntimeNodePort(
647: +	ctx context.Context,
648: +	nodeName string,
649: +	port int,
650: +) (net.Conn, error) {
651: +	forwarder, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodePortForwarder](
652: +		c, "port-forwarding to nodes")
653: +	if err != nil {
654: +		return nil, err
655: +	}
656: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
657: +		return nil, err
658: +	}
659: +
660: +	return forwarder.DialPort(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
661: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
662: +		Nodes:    []string{nodeName},
663: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
664: +	}, port)
665: +}
666: +
667: +// SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats reports the CPU and memory usage of the lab's running nodes. It
668: +// returns an error wrapping labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable when the cluster serves no resource
669: +// metrics.
670: +func (c *CLab) SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats(ctx context.Context) ([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, error) {
671: +	sampler, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeStatsSampler](
672: +		c, "sampling node stats")
673: +	if err != nil {
674: +		return nil, err
675: +	}
676: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
677: +		return nil, err
678: +	}
679: +
680: +	return sampler.SampleStats(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
681: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
682: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
683: +	})
684: +}
685: +
686: +// NodeLogOptions selects the node log NodeLogs writes.
687: +type NodeLogOptions struct {
688: +	// NodeName is the node whose log is written.
689: +	NodeName string
690: +	// Container overrides a lab runtime node's primary device container. Local runtimes do
691: +	// not support it.
692: +	Container string
693: +	// Tail limits the output to the last lines of the log; nil writes the whole log.
694: +	Tail *int64
695: +	// Follow keeps writing new log lines until the context ends.
696: +	Follow bool
697: +	// Timestamps prefixes every line with its timestamp.
698: +	Timestamps bool
699: +}
700: +
701: +// NodeLogs writes the log of a lab node with every runtime: the container log with Docker and
702: +// Podman, the device container log with a lab runtime. Lab runtimes write one combined stream to
703: +// stdout.
704: +func (c *CLab) NodeLogs(
705: +	ctx context.Context,
706: +	opts NodeLogOptions,
707: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
708: +) error {
709: +	if opts.NodeName == "" {
710: +		return fmt.Errorf("node name is required")
711: +	}
712: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
713: +		return err
714: +	}
715: +
716: +	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
717: +		streamer, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLogStreamer](
718: +			c, "streaming node logs")
719: +		if err != nil {
720: +			return err
721: +		}
722: +
723: +		return streamer.StreamLogs(ctx, clablabruntime.LogRequest{
724: +			Name:       c.Config.Name,
725: +			NodeName:   opts.NodeName,
726: +			Container:  opts.Container,
727: +			Tail:       opts.Tail,
728: +			Follow:     opts.Follow,
729: +			Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
730: +			Identity:   c.labRuntimeIdentity,
731: +		}, stdout)
732: +	}
733: +
734: +	if opts.Container != "" {
735: +		return fmt.Errorf("selecting a container is only supported with lab runtimes")
736: +	}
737: +
738: +	runtime, containerName, err := c.nodeContainer(ctx, opts.NodeName)
739: +	if err != nil {
740: +		return err
741: +	}
742: +
743: +	writer, ok := runtime.(clabruntime.ContainerLogWriter)
744: +	if !ok {
745: +		return fmt.Errorf("container runtime %q does not support node logs", runtime.GetName())
746: +	}
747: +
748: +	return writer.WriteContainerLogs(ctx, containerName, clabruntime.ContainerLogOptions{
749: +		Tail:       opts.Tail,
750: +		Follow:     opts.Follow,
751: +		Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
752: +	}, stdout, stderr)
753: +}
754: +
755: +// nodeContainer finds the container of a lab node in the local container runtimes by the lab
756: +// and node name labels.
757: +func (c *CLab) nodeContainer(
758: +	ctx context.Context,
759: +	nodeName string,
760: +) (clabruntime.ContainerRuntime, string, error) {
761: +	filters := []*clabtypes.GenericFilter{
762: +		{
763: +			FilterType: "label",
764: +			Field:      clabconstants.Containerlab,
765: +			Operator:   "=",
766: +			Match:      c.Config.Name,
767: +		},
768: +		{
769: +			FilterType: "label",
770: +			Field:      clabconstants.NodeName,
771: +			Operator:   "=",
772: +			Match:      nodeName,
773: +		},
774: +	}
775: +
776: +	runtimeNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Runtimes))
777: +	for name := range c.Runtimes {
778: +		runtimeNames = append(runtimeNames, name)
779: +	}
780: +	sort.Strings(runtimeNames)
781: +
782: +	for _, name := range runtimeNames {
783: +		runtime := c.Runtimes[name]
784: +
785: +		containers, err := runtime.ListContainers(ctx, filters)
786: +		if err != nil {
787: +			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("could not list containers: %w", err)
788: +		}
789: +		if len(containers) != 0 && len(containers[0].Names) != 0 {
790: +			return runtime, containers[0].Names[0], nil
791: +		}
792: +	}
793: +
794: +	return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: node %q of lab %q has no container",
795: +		ErrNodeNotFound, nodeName, c.Config.Name)
796: +}
797: +
798: +func (c *CLab) requireLabName() error {
799: +	if c.Config == nil || c.Config.Name == "" {
800: +		return fmt.Errorf("provide a lab name (--name) or a topology file (--topo)")
801: +	}
802: +
803: +	return nil
804: +}
805: +
806: +// labRuntimeCapability returns the CLab's lab runtime as an optional lab runtime interface.
807: +func labRuntimeCapability[T any](c *CLab, operation string) (T, error) {
808: +	var zero T
809: +
810: +	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
811: +		return zero, fmt.Errorf("%s needs a lab runtime such as %q",
812: +			operation, clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName)
813: +	}
814: +
815: +	capability, ok := c.LabRuntime.(T)
816: +	if !ok {
817: +		return zero, fmt.Errorf("lab runtime %q does not support %s",
818: +			c.globalRuntimeName, operation)
819: +	}
820: +
821: +	return capability, nil
822: +}

1042: +func TestNodeLogsWithALocalRuntime(t *testing.T) {
1043: +	t.Parallel()
1044: +
1045: +	ctrl := gomock.NewController(t)
1046: +	mock := clabmocksmockruntime.NewMockContainerRuntime(ctrl)
1047: +	mock.EXPECT().ListContainers(gomock.Any(), gomock.Any()).DoAndReturn(
1048: +		func(_ context.Context, filters []*clabtypes.GenericFilter) (
1049: +			[]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error,
1050: +		) {
1051: +			labels := map[string]string{}
1052: +			for _, filter := range filters {
1053: +				labels[filter.Field] = filter.Match
1054: +			}
1055: +			if labels[clabconstants.Containerlab] != "lab1" {
1056: +				return nil, nil
1057: +			}
1058: +			if labels[clabconstants.NodeName] != "r1" {
1059: +				return nil, nil
1060: +			}
1061: +
1062: +			return []clabruntime.GenericContainer{{Names: []string{"clab-lab1-r1"}}}, nil
1063: +		}).
1064: +		AnyTimes()
1065: +
1066: +	runtime := &logWritingRuntime{MockContainerRuntime: mock}
1067: +	c := &CLab{
1068: +		Config:   &Config{Name: "lab1"},
1069: +		Runtimes: map[string]clabruntime.ContainerRuntime{"docker": runtime},
1070: +	}
1071: +
1072: +	var stdout, stderr strings.Builder
1073: +	if err := c.NodeLogs(context.Background(), NodeLogOptions{NodeName: "r1", Follow: true},
1074: +		&stdout, &stderr); err != nil {
1075: +		t.Fatal(err)
1076: +	}
1077: +	if runtime.containerName != "clab-lab1-r1" || !runtime.opts.Follow ||
1078: +		runtime.opts.Tail != nil ||
1079: +		stdout.String() != "out\n" ||
1080: +		stderr.String() != "err\n" {

1087: +	if !errors.Is(err, ErrNodeNotFound) {

1089: +	}
1090: +
1091: +	if err := c.NodeLogs(context.Background(), NodeLogOptions{NodeName: "r1", Container: "x"},
1092: +		io.Discard, io.Discard); err == nil {
1093: +		t.Fatal("a container override was accepted for a local runtime")
1094: +	}
1095: +}

Node names are accepted as the topology file spells\n+// them or as a lab runtime sanitized them. Lab runtime calls act as the identity set with\n+// WithLabRuntimeIdentity.\n+\n+// LocateLabRuntimeNodes reports the workload (namespace, pod, primary device container, Node\n+// UID, exposed ports) of the given nodes, or of every node of the lab when none are given.\n+func (c *CLab) LocateLabRuntimeNodes(\n+\tctx context.Context,\n+\tnodeNames ...string,\n+) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {\n+\tlocator, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLocator](c, \"locating nodes\")\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn nil, err\n+\t}\n+\tif err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {\n+\t\treturn nil, err\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn locator.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{\n+\t\tName:     c.Config.Name,\n+\t\tNodes:    nodeNames,\n+\t\tIdentity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,\n+\t})\n+}\n+\n+// AttachLabRuntimeNode runs an interactive command in a node's device container (or in\n+// req.Container) with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing. The lab name and identity\n+// default to the CLab's. A command exiting nonzero returns a *labruntime.CommandExitError.\n+func (c *CLab) AttachLabRuntimeNode(\n+\tctx context.Context,\n+\treq clablabruntime.AttachRequest,\n+\tstreams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,\n+) error {\n+\tattacher, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeAttacher](c, \"attaching to nodes\")\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn err\n+\t}\n+\n+\tif req.Name == \"\" {\n+\t\tif err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {\n+\t\t\treturn err\n+\t\t}\n+\t\treq.Name = c.Config.Name\n+\t}\n+\tif req.Identity.IsZero() {\n+\t\treq.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn attacher.Attach(ctx, req, streams)\n+}\n+\n+// DialLabRuntimeNodePort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node (SSH, web UIs) through the\n+// lab runtime, such as a Kubernetes port-forward.\n+func (c *CLab) DialLabRuntimeNodePort(\n+\tctx context.Context,\n+\tnodeName string,\n+\tport int,\n+) (net.Conn, error) {\n+\tforwarder, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodePortForwarder](\n+\t\tc, \"port-forwarding to nodes\")\n+\tif err != nil {\n+\t\treturn nil, err\n+\t}\n+\tif err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {\n+\t\treturn nil, err\n+\t}\n+\n+\treturn forwarder.DialPort(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{\n+\t\tName:     c.Config.Name,\n+\t\tNodes:    []string{nodeName},\n+\t\tIdentity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,\n+\t}, port)\n+}\n+\n+// SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats reports the CPU and memory usage of the lab's running nodes. 1351: @@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
1352: +# logs command
1353: +
1354: +### Description
1355: +
1356: +The `logs` command shows the log of a lab node. With Docker and Podman it is the node container's log, with the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#logs) the log of the node's primary device container in its pod.
1357: +
1358: +--8<-- "docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags"
1359: +
1360: +### Usage
1361: +
1362: +`containerlab [global-flags] logs [local-flags]`
1363: +
1364: +### Flags
1365: +
1366: +#### topology | name
1367: +
1368: +Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.
1369: +
1370: +#### node
1371: +
1372: +Use the local `--node | -n` flag to select the node. The flag is required. With the c9s runtime the node name is accepted as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`).
1373: +
1374: +#### tail
1375: +
1376: +The local `--tail` flag limits the output to the last N lines of the log. The default `-1` shows the whole log; `--tail 0` shows no previous lines, which is useful with `--follow`.
1377: +
1378: +#### follow
1379: +
1380: +The local `--follow | -f` flag keeps streaming new log lines until the command is interrupted.
1381: +
1382: +#### timestamps
1383: +
1384: +The local `--timestamps` flag prefixes every line with its timestamp in RFC 3339 format.
1385: +
1386: +### Output
1387: +
1388: +The log goes to stdout. With Docker and Podman, the container's stderr goes to stderr, unless the container has a TTY; Kubernetes returns one combined stream, written to stdout.
1389: +
1390: +### Examples
1391: +
1392: +#### Show the whole log of a node
1393: +
1394: +```bash
1395: +containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1
1396: +```
1397: +
1398: +#### Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps
1399: +
1400: +```bash
1401: +containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps
1402: +```
1403: +
1404: +#### Show the device log of a node in a c9s lab
1405: +
1406: +```bash
1407: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 50
1408: +```

1410: index 88e63a4..18dc015 100644
1411: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
1412: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
1413: @@ -528,10 +528,24 @@ needs to reach the cluster.
1414:  If any selected command returns nonzero, or pod exec itself fails, the outer
1415:  `containerlab exec` also returns nonzero. Successful and failed results that
1416:  were received are still printed, so automation can use both the output and the
1417:  process exit status.
1418:  
1419: +## Logs
1420: +
1421: +`logs` shows the log of a node's primary device container, the same container
1422: +`exec` uses:
1423: +
1424: +```bash
1425: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs -t topo.clab.yml -n srl1
1426: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps
1427: +```
1428: +
1429: +It reads the `pods/log` subresource of the node's pod, so RBAC must allow
1430: +`get` on `pods/log`. Kubernetes returns stdout and stderr as one stream. See
1431: +the [`logs` command](../../cmd/logs.md) for the flags.
1432: +
1433:  ## Start, stop, and restart
1434:  
1435:  Node lifecycle commands operate on the kubernetes Deployments created by
1436:  Clabernetes.
1437:  
1438: @@ -782,10 +796,66 @@ token:
1439:  ```bash
1440:  kubectl -n <namespace> annotate node.c9s.run <node> \
1441:    c9s.run/device-state-reset=$(date +%s) --overwrite
1442:  ```
1443:  
1444: +## Node access from Go
1445: +
1446: +Programs that use containerlab as a Go library, such as clab-api-server, open
1447: +terminals, follow logs, reach node ports and read resource usage through
1448: +optional lab runtime interfaces in `github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime`,
1449: +implemented by the c9s runtime:
1450: +
1451: +| Interface | Method | What it does |
1452: +|---|---|---|
1453: +| `NodeLocator` | `LocateNode(ctx, NodeRequest) ([]NodeLocation, error)` | the namespace, pod, primary device container, Node UID, exposed ports and LoadBalancer address of nodes |
1454: +| `NodeAttacher` | `Attach(ctx, AttachRequest, AttachStreams) error` | an interactive exec with stdin, an optional TTY and a resize channel, in the device container or a chosen container |
1455: +| `NodeLogStreamer` | `StreamLogs(ctx, LogRequest, io.Writer) error` | the device container log, with tail, follow and timestamps |
1456: +| `NodePortForwarder` | `DialPort(ctx, NodeRequest, port) (net.Conn, error)` | a connection to a TCP port of the node's pod through `pods/portforward` (SSH, web UIs) |
1457: +| `NodeStatsSampler` | `SampleStats(ctx, InspectRequest) ([]NodeStats, error)` | CPU and memory per node from `metrics.k8s.io` PodMetrics, summing the node's device containers; without the metrics API the error wraps `labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable` |
1458: +
1459: +The `core` package wraps them per lab and node name, accepting the node name
1460: +as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized:
1461: +`CLab.LocateLabRuntimeNodes`, `CLab.AttachLabRuntimeNode`,
1462: +`CLab.DialLabRuntimeNodePort`, `CLab.SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats` and
1463: +`CLab.NodeLogs`, which also serves Docker and Podman.
1464: +
1465: +```go
1466: +c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(
1467: +	clabcore.WithRuntime("c9s", nil),
1468: +	clabcore.WithTopologyName("clos"),
1469: +	clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity(clablabruntime.Identity{
1470: +		User:   "clab:alice",
1471: +		Groups: []string{"clab:users"},
1472: +	}),
1473: +)
1474: +if err != nil {
1475: +	return err
1476: +}
1477: +
1478: +conn, err := c.DialLabRuntimeNodePort(ctx, "srl1", 22)
1479: +```
1480: +
1481: +### Acting as a user
1482: +
1483: +A server that runs labs for many users acts as each user, so the cluster's RBAC
1484: +decides what a user may do and its audit log names the user:
1485: +
1486: +- `labruntime.Identity{User, Groups}` is Kubernetes user impersonation.
1487: +  `labruntime.Config.Identity` sets it for a runtime, every request type has an
1488: +  `Identity` field that overrides it per call, and
1489: +  `clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity` sets it for every call of a `CLab`.
1490: +- The c9s runtime builds one set of Kubernetes clients per identity from the
1491: +  kubeconfig and caches them. The impersonation applies to every transport:
1492: +  REST calls, watches, log streams, and the websocket and SPDY connections of
1493: +  exec, attach and port-forward.
1494: +- Without an identity, the kubeconfig is used as it is. The CLI has no
1495: +  impersonation flags: a CLI user acts with their own kubeconfig rights.
1496: +
1497: +The kubeconfig identity then needs the `impersonate` verb on the users and
1498: +groups it acts as.
1499: +
1500:  ## RBAC requirements
1501:  
1502:  The kube identity used by the outer containerlab process must be able to:
1503:  
1504:  - get, create, and delete namespaces when using automatic per-lab namespaces
1505: @@ -796,10 +866,13 @@ The kube identity used by the outer containerlab process must be able to:
1506:  - list and watch Pods
1507:  - list, get, and update Deployments
1508:  - create, get, list, update, and delete ConfigMaps used for local files
1509:  - exec into device Pods with `pods/exec`
1510:  - list and delete PersistentVolumeClaims for `destroy --cleanup`
1511: +- read container logs with `pods/log` for `logs`
1512: +- port-forward with `pods/portforward` for `NodePortForwarder`
1513: +- list `pods.metrics.k8s.io` for `NodeStatsSampler`
1514:  
1515:  Useful checks:
1516:  
1517:  ```bash
1518:  kubectl auth can-i get namespaces

The default `-1` shows the whole log; `--tail 0` shows no previous lines, which is useful with `--follow`.\n+\n+#### follow\n+\n+The local `--follow | -f` flag keeps streaming new log lines until the command is interrupted.\n+\n+#### timestamps\n+\n+The local `--timestamps` flag prefixes every line with its timestamp in RFC 3339 format.\n+\n+### Output\n+\n+The log goes to stdout. 1693: +// Attach runs an interactive command in a node's device container, or in the container the
1694: +// request names, with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing.
1695: +func (r *Runtime) Attach(
1696: +	ctx context.Context,
1697: +	req clablabruntime.AttachRequest,
1698: +	streams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,
1699: +) error {
1700: +	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
1701: +	if err != nil {
1702: +		return err
1703: +	}
1704: +
1705: +	location, err := r.runningNode(ctx, req.Name, req.Namespace, req.NodeName)
1706: +	if err != nil {
1707: +		return err
1708: +	}
1709: +
1710: +	container := req.Container
1711: +	if container == "" {
1712: +		container = location.Container
1713: +	}
1714: +	command := req.Command
1715: +	if len(command) == 0 {
1716: +		command = defaultAttachCommand
1717: +	}
1718: +
1719: +	stderr := streams.Stderr
1720: +	if req.TTY {
1721: +		// a terminal merges stderr into stdout
1722: +		stderr = nil
1723: +	}
1724: +
1725: +	execURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
1726: +		Resource("pods").
1727: +		Name(location.Pod).
1728: +		Namespace(location.Namespace).
1729: +		SubResource("exec").
1730: +		VersionedParams(&corev1.PodExecOptions{
1731: +			Container: container,
1732: +			Command:   command,
1733: +			Stdin:     streams.Stdin != nil,
1734: +			Stdout:    streams.Stdout != nil,
1735: +			Stderr:    stderr != nil,
1736: +			TTY:       req.TTY,
1737: +		}, scheme.ParameterCodec).URL()
1738: +
1739: +	executor, err := r.newExecutor(execURL)
1740: +	if err != nil {
1741: +		return err
1742: +	}
1743: +
1744: +	options := remotecommand.StreamOptions{
1745: +		Stdin:  streams.Stdin,
1746: +		Stdout: streams.Stdout,
1747: +		Stderr: stderr,
1748: +		Tty:    req.TTY,
1749: +	}
1750: +	if req.TTY && streams.Resize != nil {
1751: +		options.TerminalSizeQueue = newTerminalSizeQueue(ctx, streams.Resize)
1752: +	}
1753: +
1754: +	err = executor.StreamWithContext(ctx, options)
1755: +
1756: +	var exitErr kubeexec.ExitError
1757: +	if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
1758: +		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: exitErr.ExitStatus()}
1759: +	}
1760: +	if err != nil {
1761: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to attach to c9s node %s/%s/%s: %w",
1762: +			location.Namespace, req.Name, location.NodeName, err)
1763: +	}
1764: +
1765: +	return nil
1766: +}
1767: +
1768: +// newExecutor streams a pod exec over websockets, falling back to SPDY when the API server
1769: +// does not upgrade the websocket, like kubectl. The websocket executor reports upgrade
1770: +// failures with the k8s.io/streaming error types. Both transports are built from the runtime's
1771: +// rest config, so they carry its impersonation headers.
1772: +func (r *Runtime) newExecutor(execURL *url.URL) (remotecommand.Executor, error) {
1773: +	websocketExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewWebSocketExecutor(
1774: +		r.restConfig, http.MethodGet, execURL.String())
1775: +	if err != nil {
1776: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes websocket exec executor: %w", err)
1777: +	}
1778: +
1779: +	spdyExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewSPDYExecutor(r.restConfig, http.MethodPost, execURL)
1780: +	if err != nil {
1781: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes exec executor: %w", err)
1782: +	}
1783: +
1784: +	return remotecommand.NewFallbackExecutor(websocketExecutor, spdyExecutor,
1785: +		func(err error) bool {
1786: +			return streamhttp.IsUpgradeFailure(err) || streamhttp.IsHTTPSProxyError(err)
1787: +		})
1788: +}

1790: +// terminalSizeQueue adapts a resize channel to the remotecommand size queue.
1791: +type terminalSizeQueue struct {
1792: +	ctx    context.Context
1793: +	resize <-chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize
1794: +}
1795: +
1796: +func newTerminalSizeQueue(
1797: +	ctx context.Context,
1798: +	resize <-chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize,
1799: +) *terminalSizeQueue {
1800: +	return &terminalSizeQueue{ctx: ctx, resize: resize}
1801: +}
1802: +
1803: +// Next blocks until the next size change; nil ends resizing.
1804: +func (q *terminalSizeQueue) Next() *remotecommand.TerminalSize {
1805: +	select {
1806: +	case <-q.ctx.Done():
1807: +		return nil
1808: +	case size, ok := <-q.resize:
1809: +		if !ok {
1810: +			return nil
1811: +		}
1812: +
1813: +		return &remotecommand.TerminalSize{Width: size.Width, Height: size.Height}
1814: +	}
1815: +}

1853: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to stream the log of c9s node %s/%s/%s: %w",
1854: +			location.Namespace, req.Name, location.NodeName, err)
